docs.title: Index
docs.text:
BirdBox

Deep Learning Bird Call Detection & Evaluation System

BirdBox is a comprehensive system for detecting and evaluating bird calls in audio recordings using deep learning. It leverages YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection on spectrogram images to identify and localize bird vocalizations in time and frequency.

⚠️ Note: This project is still under active development. Performance may vary.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This code repository focuses on model inference and post-processing for bioacoustic event detection. Additionally, one can evaluate the performance of the model inference with ground truth annotations. Metrics like precision, recall, F\(\beta\) and confusion matrices are already implemented and ready to go.

What's not covered here is the model training. For this see BirdBox-Train (currently only available from within the BirdNET-Team).

docs.title: Example Detection
docs.text:
The image shows 15 seconds of a soundscape from Hawai'i (tests/test.wav, 195 to 210 s) as the model sees it: the log-floor mel spectrogram from 50 Hz to 15 kHz. The boxes are the detections of Just-Bird with the default settings, each with its confidence. Each box localizes a call or a phrase in time and frequency.

Spectrogram Not Stored

The inference software takes in audio files and outputs detections in various formats. The spectrogram is computed internally but never written to disk unless explicitly visualized.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Browser Demo - Runs Just-Bird or Birds-With-Labels in the browser, with no installation
  • Multiple Audio Formats - Supports WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 (WAV/FLAC recommended for best results)
  • Arbitrary-Length Audio Processing - Handle audio from seconds to hours
  • Window Fusion and Song Reconstruction - Merge the boxes of overlapping windows into calls or phrases, or adjacent detections into continuous songs
  • Batch Processing - Process entire directories of audio files
  • Log-Floor Spectrograms - Log power above each band's noise floor, independent of the recording level
  • Comprehensive Evaluation - F-beta analysis, confusion matrices, optimal threshold finding
  • Multiple Output Formats - JSON with algorithm metadata, simplified CSV, xeno-canto Annota-JSON and Raven Selection Table
  • Multiple Model Formats - Works with .pt, .onnx and .tflite model formats

docs.title: License
docs.text:
BirdBox's own source code is licensed under the MIT License.

BirdBox is built on Ultralytics YOLO11, which is licensed under the AGPL-3.0. Ultralytics also treats models trained or fine-tuned with it as AGPL-3.0, so the BirdBox model weights (.pt and every exported format) are AGPL-3.0 as well. As a result, the project as a whole is subject to the AGPL-3.0:

  • Using BirdBox with Ultralytics or the BirdBox models (running, redistributing, or offering it over a network) has to comply with the AGPL-3.0. If you modify it and let users interact with it over a network, you must offer them its source code.
  • Reusing BirdBox's own code on its own, in a project that uses neither Ultralytics nor the BirdBox models, is possible under the MIT terms.

A few files are under other licenses (a function adapted from librosa, xeno-canto audio samples, AviList-derived taxonomy data). See NOTICE.md for the full breakdown.

docs.title: About this demo
docs.text:
Three pages in How It Works describe the demo. Detection explains how it detects and where its limits are. Spectrogram explains its two spectrograms. Adding Models explains how to add a model to the menu.

The sample soundscape is the example recording of BirdNET-Analyzer (birdnet_analyzer/example/soundscape.wav, MIT License), resampled to 32 kHz. The BirdNET website demo uses the same file. Recordings loaded by their XC number come from Xeno-canto under the license of each recording.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Installing BirdBox takes about ten minutes. Most of that time goes to large libraries such as PyTorch and Ultralytics.

The install.py script detects your hardware and installs the matching packages. Pass --model-format to install the runtime for a model format. Without it, the script installs support for .pt models.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12. install.py exits on any other version.
    • On Windows and macOS, use the installer of Python 3.12.10. It is the last 3.12 release with installers. On Windows, keep the py launcher option selected, because the commands below use it.
    • On Linux, install Python 3.12 with your package manager or with pyenv. On Debian and Ubuntu, also install the python3.12-venv package. Without it, creating the environment fails.
    • The plain python command is often a different version. So the commands below call Python 3.12 explicitly: python3.12 on Linux and macOS, py -3.12 on Windows.
  • macOS works on Apple Silicon (M1 and later) only. PyTorch 2.5.1 and ONNX Runtime 1.27.0 publish no packages for Intel Macs.
  • Disk space depends on the format and on whether CUDA libraries are included. Measured sizes of the environment: about 2 GB for tflite and CPU-only installs, about 6.5 GB for pt and onnx with CUDA, and about 13 GB for engine.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
• An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA makes inference much faster. Without one, BirdBox runs on the CPU, which takes considerably longer on large files.
  • install.py looks for an NVIDIA GPU with nvidia-smi. If it finds one, it installs CUDA packages. Otherwise it installs CPU packages.
  • Macs always get CPU packages and run inference on the CPU. The Apple GPU (MPS) is not used.
  • The NVIDIA driver must be new enough for the CUDA version of your format. The Model Formats table lists the minimum driver versions.

docs.title: Installation Commands
docs.text:
Copy the commands for your operating system. They create a virtual environment named .venv and run install.py inside it. The pipeline scripts (run_pipeline.sh, run_pipeline.ps1, run_pipeline.bat) activate .venv by themselves if it exists. Without .venv, they use the Python that is active.

Without Git, download the repository from GitHub as a ZIP file (Code, then Download ZIP), unpack it and start at step 2.

Add --model-format <FORMAT> to the last command to install a runtime other than .pt. See Install Parameters for all options.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD)Conda 
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/birdnet-team/BirdBox.git
cd BirdBox

# 2. Create a virtual environment with Python 3.12
python3.12 -m venv .venv

# 3. Activate the environment
source .venv/bin/activate

# 4. Install dependencies  (add --model-format <FORMAT> to change the runtime)
python install.py

# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/birdnet-team/BirdBox.git
cd BirdBox

# 2. Create a virtual environment with Python 3.12
py -3.12 -m venv .venv

# 3. Activate the environment
#    If PowerShell refuses to run the script, first run:
#    Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process RemoteSigned
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# 4. Install dependencies  (add --model-format <FORMAT> to change the runtime)
python install.py

PowerShell runs script files only if its execution policy allows them. The default on Windows desktops blocks all scripts. Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process RemoteSigned allows local scripts in the current window only. It needs no admin rights and resets when you close the window. The same applies to run_pipeline.ps1. If you downloaded the repository as a ZIP file, Windows marks run_pipeline.ps1 as downloaded, and RemoteSigned still blocks it. Run Unblock-File run_pipeline.ps1 once to remove the mark.

rem 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/birdnet-team/BirdBox.git
cd BirdBox

rem 2. Create a virtual environment with Python 3.12
py -3.12 -m venv .venv

rem 3. Activate the environment
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat

rem 4. Install dependencies  (add --model-format <FORMAT> to change the runtime)
python install.py

# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/birdnet-team/BirdBox.git
cd BirdBox

# 2. Create a conda environment with Python 3.12
conda create -n birdbox python=3.12

# 3. Activate the environment
conda activate birdbox

# 4. Install dependencies  (add --model-format <FORMAT> to change the runtime)
python install.py

The pipeline scripts do not activate conda environments. Activate the environment yourself before you run them.

docs.title: Check the Installation
docs.text:
Run this in the activated environment:

python -c "import torch, ultralytics; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())"

It prints the PyTorch version and whether PyTorch can use the GPU. On an NVIDIA system with a CUDA install, the output ends with True. On a Mac or with a CPU install, it ends with False.

Next, download a model and run a first detection as in Simple Workflow for Detection Only.

docs.title: Install Parameters
docs.text:
install.py accepts two optional arguments. A plain python install.py sets up .pt support and detects the GPU.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --model-format CHOICE / pt No Model format to install the inference runtime for. Each value installs a different set of packages. --mode CHOICE / auto No Compute mode for PyTorch and ONNX Runtime. auto installs CUDA packages when nvidia-smi finds an NVIDIA GPU. cpu forces CPU packages. cuda forces CUDA packages, for example when nvidia-smi is not on the PATH.

.tflite models always run on the CPU. So with --model-format tflite, auto installs CPU PyTorch even on NVIDIA systems. --mode cuda still installs CUDA PyTorch, which .tflite models do not use.

docs.title: Model Formats
docs.text:
Every environment gets the packages in requirements.txt. These include onnx and onnxslim, which BirdBox uses to read and export ONNX models. Each format adds its runtime on top.

--model-format Model file Runtime installed Platform pt (default) .pt PyTorch. CUDA 11.8 build on NVIDIA systems, needs driver 450 or newer. Any onnx .onnx PyTorch and ONNX Runtime. CUDA 12.1 PyTorch on NVIDIA systems, needs driver 525 or newer. Any tflite .tflite CPU PyTorch and ai-edge-litert Any engine .engine CUDA 12.1 PyTorch, tensorrt-cu12 11.1 and ONNX Runtime NVIDIA GPU required

An environment runs .pt models and the format it was installed for. An engine environment also runs .onnx models. Loading any other format stops with an error that names the install command. To use a second format, create a second environment, for example .venv-onnx, and run install.py with that format in it.

Conversion benchmarks for the model types are given at Birds-With-Labels-Model-Types and Just-Bird-Model-Types.

Platform Restrictions

--model-format engine requires an NVIDIA GPU and will exit with an error on CPU-only or macOS machines.

TensorRT is pinned to version 11.1.0.106. A .engine file only loads in the TensorRT version that built it, so build your engines in this environment.

GPU compute for ONNX models

Ultralytics runs .onnx models through ONNX Runtime. It only uses the GPU when PyTorch has CUDA as well. So on NVIDIA systems, --model-format onnx installs CUDA PyTorch next to onnxruntime-gpu. install.py tries two ONNX Runtime builds and keeps the first one that runs on the GPU:

  1. onnxruntime-gpu 1.27.0 with its own CUDA 13 libraries. It needs driver 580 or newer.
  2. onnxruntime-gpu 1.26.0 with CUDA 12 libraries, which it shares with PyTorch. It needs driver 525 or newer.

If neither works, the script removes the ONNX Runtime GPU packages and installs CPU onnxruntime. .onnx models then run on the CPU. PyTorch keeps CUDA, so .pt models in the same environment still use the GPU.

CLI models and the demo graph

--model-format onnx is for network-only ONNX exports, as made by the Ultralytics exporter. They take a spectrogram image and return raw YOLO output, and detect_birds.py does the pre- and postprocessing in Python. The Demo graph (docs/models/*.onnx, built by src/inference/onnx_export.py) is a different artefact. It takes raw audio and returns merged detections, with the log-floor spectrogram, NMS and merging inside the graph. It only needs an ONNX runtime and cannot be loaded by detect_birds.py.

docs.title: Model Download
docs.text: The YOLO models are not included in the BirdBox repository. Download only the models you need. Store them in the models/ directory of your clone, where the pipeline scripts and the examples in these docs expect them.

docs.title: TUC-Cloud
docs.text: Trained YOLO models can be found on the TUC-Cloud. Each model has its own folder there. File names carry the weight data type: .pt comes as fp32, .onnx and .tflite as fp16 and int8. Start with Just-Bird_fp32.pt from the Just-Bird folder. Just-Bird is the recommended model. The examples in these docs expect it at models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt. For details see Models and Metrics.

docs.title: GitHub Releases
docs.text:
Each BirdBox release has the model files it was released with attached as assets, with the same names as on the TUC-Cloud. The TUC-Cloud always has the current files and may be updated later. A release keeps its files unchanged. Download from the release to work with exactly the weights of a given BirdBox version, for example to reproduce published results.

SHA256SUMS.txt in each release lists the checksum of every model file. To check downloaded files, run this in the folder that holds them:

LinuxmacOSWindows (PowerShell) 
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing

Each checked file should report OK.

shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing

Each checked file should report OK.

Get-FileHash Just-Bird_fp32.pt -Algorithm SHA256

Compare the printed hash with the line for that file in SHA256SUMS.txt.

docs.title: Custom Model Training
docs.text:
Alternatively, train your own model on a custom dataset using BirdBox-Train.

Restricted Access

BirdBox-Train is currently only available to members of the BirdNET Team.

docs.title: API Type
docs.text:
BirdBox is a Python library. There is no server, no HTTP endpoint, and no REST API. You import the classes directly into your own Python scripts and call them as regular functions.

from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector   # local Python import

If you are looking for a point-and-click interface or want to run detection without writing code, use the CLI Reference or the Demo instead.

docs.title: Module Overview
docs.text: Module Key class / function What it does inference.detect_birds BirdCallDetector Load a model and run detection on audio files evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis FBetaScoreAnalyzer Sweep confidence thresholds, compute F-beta scores evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections DetectionFilter Filter raw detections by confidence and merge them evaluation.confusion_matrix_analysis ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer Build a per-species confusion matrix

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Make sure the BirdBox environment is set up and your working directory is the project root before importing:

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "src")   # BirdBox is not a pip package, so add src/ to the import path

from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

See Installation for the full setup instructions.

docs.title: Confusion Matrix Analysis
docs.text: Compute a confusion matrix comparing filtered detection results against ground truth labels. Matches detections to labels using IoU with the Hungarian (optimal) algorithm, then builds a per-species confusion matrix showing correct classifications, misclassifications, false positives, and false negatives.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from evaluation.confusion_matrix_analysis import ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer(
    iou_threshold=0.25,
    use_2d_iou=True,
    include_background=True,
    single_cls=False,
    single_cls_name="bird",
)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description iou_threshold float / 0.25 No IoU threshold for matching a detection to a ground truth label. Use the same value as in FBetaScoreAnalyzer for consistent evaluation. use_2d_iou bool / True No If True, uses 2D IoU (time and frequency). If False, uses 1D IoU (time overlap only). 2D IoU is more accurate. Use 1D only when frequency annotations are unreliable or absent. include_background bool / True No If True, adds a background class for unmatched detections (FP) and unmatched labels (FN). Pass False to see only species-vs-species misclassifications. single_cls bool / False No Collapse all species into one class for binary bird-detection evaluation. Use it for Just-Bird. single_cls_name str / 'bird' No Class name to use when single_cls=True.

The single-class matrix

With single_cls=True and the background class, the matrix is 2×2: [[TP, FP], [FN, 0]]. Rows are bird and background as predicted, columns the same as annotated. The background-background cell is always 0, because there are no true negatives in event detection. With include_background=False, only the TP cell remains.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description analyze(detections_path, labels_path, output_path) Tuple[np.ndarray, List[str]] Run the full analysis. Primary entry point. load_detections_csv(detections_path) List[Dict] Load merged detections CSV. load_labels_csv(labels_path) List[Dict] Load ground truth labels CSV. compute_confusion_matrix(detections, labels) Tuple[np.ndarray, List[str]] Build the matrix from loaded data. save_results(confusion_matrix, species_list, output_path, detections_path=None, labels_path=None, num_detections=None, num_labels=None) None Write CSV, images, and metadata. The paths and counts go into metadata.txt.

docs.title: The analyze Method
docs.text:
matrix, species = analyzer.analyze(
    detections_path,
    labels_path,
    output_path=None,
)

Run the complete confusion matrix pipeline: load, match, compute, optionally save.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections_path str / none Yes Path to the simplified.csv file from DetectionFilter. Only the CLI resolves a results/ directory and follows .active_run. labels_path str / none Yes Path to the ground truth labels CSV. Must use the same six-column schema as the detections file. output_path str / None No Directory for output files. When provided, writes the confusion matrix CSV, heatmap images, and metadata.

Returns: (np.ndarray, List[str]). The confusion matrix and the ordered species list.

docs.title: The load_detections_csv Method
docs.text:
detections = analyzer.load_detections_csv(detections_path)

Load a simplified.csv produced by DetectionFilter. Returns a list of dicts with keys filename, time_start, time_end, freq_low_hz, freq_high_hz, species.

docs.title: The load_labels_csv Method
docs.text:
labels = analyzer.load_labels_csv(labels_path)

Load a ground truth labels CSV. Returns a list of dicts with keys filename, start_time, end_time, freq_low, freq_high, species.

Label dicts use different keys than detection dicts

Detections use time_start, time_end, freq_low_hz and freq_high_hz. Labels use start_time, end_time, freq_low and freq_high. The matcher reads labels by these keys, so labels built with the detection key names fail with a TypeError during IoU computation.

docs.title: The compute_confusion_matrix Method
docs.text:
matrix, species_list = analyzer.compute_confusion_matrix(detections, labels)

Build the confusion matrix from pre-loaded data. The Hungarian algorithm [15] assigns detections to labels globally at IoU ≥ iou_threshold.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections List[Dict] / none Yes Detections from load_detections_csv(). labels List[Dict] / none Yes Labels from load_labels_csv().

Returns: (np.ndarray, List[str]). The confusion matrix and the species list. With N = len(species), the matrix shape is (N+1, N+1) when include_background=True (the last row and column are background) and (N, N) otherwise. The species list never contains background.

docs.title: IoU Matching
docs.text:
Determines how strictly a detection must overlap a ground truth label to count as a True Positive.

Value Strictness Typical use 0.1 Very lenient When annotations are coarse 0.25 (default) Moderate Good starting point for most datasets 0.5 Strict When annotations are precise and detailed

docs.title: 2D vs 1D IoU
docs.text:
2D IoU (default) measures the overlap of the two time-frequency boxes. The intersection area is divided by the union area:

\[\text{IoU}_{2D} = \frac{A_{\cap}}{A_1 + A_2 - A_{\cap}}, \qquad A_{\cap} = t_{\text{overlap}} \cdot f_{\text{overlap}}\]

Here \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) are the areas (duration × bandwidth) of the detection and the label.

1D IoU (use_2d_iou=False) measures time overlap only:

\[\text{IoU}_{1D} = \frac{t_{\text{overlap}}}{t_{\text{union}}}\]

Use use_2d_iou=False only when frequency annotations are unreliable or absent.

docs.title: Background Class
docs.text:
When include_background=True, the matrix gets an extra background row and column. Rows are the predicted class, columns are the true (annotated) class:

  • Background column: detections that did not match any ground truth label. These are False Positives.
  • Background row: ground truth labels not matched by any detection. These are False Negatives.

Set include_background=False to see only the species-level confusion (correct or wrong species label), without the FP and FN counts.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
All files are written to the output_path directory.

File Description confusion_matrix.csv Raw confusion matrix as CSV. confusion_matrix_detailed.csv Same matrix with pred_<class> rows and true_<class> columns. confusion_matrix_normalized.png Heatmap, column-normalized. Each true-class column sums to 1 and shows how that class's instances were distributed across predictions. confusion_matrix_raw.png Heatmap showing raw counts. metadata.txt Analysis parameters, file paths, species list, detection and label counts. args.yaml Every CLI argument used for this run. Written by the CLI script only.

docs.title: Reading the Confusion Matrix
docs.text:
Rows are the predicted class, columns are the true (annotated) class.

bg is the index of the background row and column. It is the last one, len(species). It exists only when the background class is included.

Cell Meaning Diagonal cell [i, i] True Positives for species i Off-diagonal [i, j] (i ≠ j) Predicted species i, actually species j (misclassification) background column [i, bg] Detections of species i that matched no label (False Positives) background row [bg, j] Labels for species j with no matching detection (False Negatives)

docs.title: Load, Compute, and Inspect in Code
docs.text:
from evaluation.confusion_matrix_analysis import ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer
import numpy as np

analyzer = ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer(iou_threshold=0.25)

detections = analyzer.load_detections_csv("results/simplified.csv")
labels = analyzer.load_labels_csv("data/annotations.csv")

matrix, species = analyzer.compute_confusion_matrix(detections, labels)

# `species` holds only real species. The background row and column are the
# extra last index, so this needs include_background=True (the default).
# Without it, matrix[i, bg] raises IndexError.
bg = len(species)
for i, sp in enumerate(species):
    tp = matrix[i, i]
    fp = matrix[i, bg]   # unmatched detections: background column
    fn = matrix[bg, i]   # unmatched labels: background row
    print(f"{sp}: TP={tp}, FP={fp}, FN={fn}")

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This class sits at Step 4 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  BirdCallDetector(conf_threshold=0.001).detect(..., no_merge=True)      ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  FBetaScoreAnalyzer().analyze_confidence_thresholds(...)                 ->  results DataFrame
        FBetaScoreAnalyzer().find_optimal_thresholds(results)                   ->  best thresholds
Step 3  DetectionFilter().filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=best_conf)     ->  merged detections
        DetectionFilter().save_results(data, merged, output_path, best_conf, None)  ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer().analyze(..., output_path=...)                 ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

Input File Format

Both detections_path and labels_path must use the six-column schema: Filename, Start Time (s), End Time (s), Low Freq (Hz), High Freq (Hz), Species eBird Code. Filenames are matched by stem only, so the extension does not matter. See CSV schema on the Ground-Truth Labels page for the full definition.

docs.title: References
docs.text: [15] Kuhn, H. W. (1955). "The Hungarian method for the assignment problem." Naval Research Logistics Quarterly, 2(1–2):83–97.

docs.title: Detecting Birds
docs.text: Detect bird calls in audio files with a trained YOLO model. BirdCallDetector processes WAV, FLAC, OGG, and MP3 files through the log-floor spectrogram pipeline. It returns time and frequency boxes with species labels and confidence scores.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector, merge_detections, reconstruct_songs, find_audio_files

docs.title: BirdCallDetector
docs.text: The main entry point for all inference workflows. Instantiate once per model, then call detect() for any number of files.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
BirdCallDetector(
    model_path,
    species_mapping,
    conf_threshold=None,
    nms_iou_threshold=0.7,
    song_gap_threshold=0.1,
    num_workers=1,
    verbose=True,
    freq_iou_threshold=None,
    merge_method=None,
    phrase_gap=None,
    label_conf=None,
)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description model_path str / none Yes Path to the trained YOLO model file (.pt, .onnx or .tflite). species_mapping str / none Yes 'Just-Bird' or 'Birds-With-Labels', the model the class IDs come from. It maps them to eBird codes and sets the default threshold. Must match the model. See Species mapping. conf_threshold float / None No Confidence threshold (0.0 to 1.0). Detections below this value are discarded. None uses the model default: 0.15 for Just-Bird and 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels. Use 0.001 to keep all raw detections for evaluation. nms_iou_threshold float / 0.7 No IoU threshold for Non-Maximum Suppression inside each 3-second clip. song_gap_threshold float / 0.1 No reconstruct merge only. Maximum gap in seconds between two detections of the same species that are still merged into one song box. num_workers int / 1 No Number of CPU processes for spectrogram features, rendering, and multi-file preprocess. YOLO inference stays in the parent and runs in batches. verbose bool / True No If True, print per-file processing details and clip-level progress bars. If False, show a single file-level progress bar. The CLI passes False unless --verbose is set. freq_iou_threshold float / None No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only: frequency IoU gate (None = 0.6, negative = time-only). merge_method str / None No 'fusion' (window ownership + weighted box fusion) or 'reconstruct' (song merge). None or 'auto' picks 'fusion' for both models. See Window fusion. phrase_gap float / None No Fusion only. Join same-band boxes closer than this many seconds into one phrase box. 0 keeps call-level boxes. None uses the model default of 0.05 s. label_conf float / None No Birds-With-Labels only. A box is named after its top species when that species' score reaches this, and bird otherwise. None uses 0.25. See Species Names.

Memory Usage

Extra workers are render processes, not extra model copies. The parent holds one YOLO model. Workers use additional RAM for matplotlib and librosa, not another set of weights.

Main entry point. detect_single_file(audio_path, progress_callback, no_merge) List[Dict] Detect in a single audio file. detect_multiple_files(audio_paths, output_path, output_formats, no_merge) List[Dict] Detect across a list of audio files. save_results(detections, output_path, audio_path, output_formats, no_merge) None Write detections to one or more output formats. merge_overlapping_detections(detections, merge_mode, file_end) List[Dict] Merge raw clip detections. load_audio(audio_path) Tuple[np.ndarray, int] Load an audio file, returns (signal, sample_rate).

docs.title: The detect Method
docs.text:
detector.detect(
    audio_path,
    output_path=None,
    output_formats=None,
    no_merge=False,
)

Detect bird calls in an audio file or directory. Automatically routes to detect_single_file() or detect_multiple_files() based on whether audio_path is a file or a directory.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description audio_path str / none Yes Path to a single audio file (WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3) or a directory. Directories are searched recursively. output_path str / None No Output directory for result files. It is created if it does not exist. If None, results are only returned, not written. output_formats List[str] / ['json-with-algorithm-metadata'] No One or more output format keys. Accepts json-with-algorithm-metadata, simplified-csv, xeno-canto-annota-json, raven-selection-table, or all. Ignored when no_merge=True. no_merge bool / False No Evaluation mode. Returns raw per-clip detections and writes only raw_detections.json. Use with conf_threshold=0.001 for F-beta sweep workflows.

Returns: List[Dict]. The merged detections, or the raw clip detections when no_merge=True.

docs.text:
detector.detect_single_file(
    audio_path,
    progress_callback=None,
    no_merge=False,
)

Detect bird calls in a single audio file. Use this method directly when you need a progress_callback (e.g. in a GUI or web app).

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description audio_path str / none Yes Path to the audio file. progress_callback Callable[[int, int, str], None] / None No Called as callback(current, total, message) after each clip. Useful for progress bars. no_merge bool / False No If True, return raw clip-level detections without merging.

Returns: List[Dict]. The detections for this file.

docs.text:
detector.save_results(
    detections,
    output_path,
    audio_path=None,
    output_formats=None,
    no_merge=False,
)

Write detections to one or more output formats under output_path.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections List[Dict] / none Yes Detections returned by detect() or detect_single_file(). output_path str / none Yes Directory to write output files into. It must exist. audio_path str / None No Source audio path, used for metadata in JSON output. output_formats List[str] / ['json-with-algorithm-metadata'] No One or more format keys (same values as detect()). no_merge bool / False No If True, writes only raw_detections.json and ignores output_formats.

docs.title: The merge_overlapping_detections Method
docs.text:
detector.merge_overlapping_detections(detections, merge_mode='reconstruct', file_end=None)

Merge raw clip detections with the detector's merge method, or remove duplicates with NMS.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections List[Dict] / none Yes Raw per-clip detections. merge_mode str / 'reconstruct' No 'reconstruct' (default) applies the detector's merge_method, which is window fusion unless you chose the song merge. detect() always uses it. 'nms' removes duplicates by IoU, keeping the highest-confidence box. file_end float / None No End of the file's last window, used by window-fusion ownership. None takes the latest clip_end among the detections.

Returns: List[Dict]. The merged or deduplicated detections.

docs.title: The merge_detections Function
docs.text:
Standalone version of the detector's merge, for raw detections saved with --no-merge. Filter by confidence first, then merge. The evaluation scripts use it, so their scores match detection.

from inference.detect_birds import file_ends_from_raw, merge_detections, resolve_merge_settings

settings = resolve_merge_settings(raw_json["model_config"])  # fusion for both models
filtered = [d for d in raw_json["detections"] if d["confidence"] >= 0.15]
merged = merge_detections(filtered, **settings, file_end=file_ends_from_raw(raw_json["detections"]))
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections List[Dict] / none Yes Raw detections with time_start, time_end, freq_low_hz, freq_high_hz, confidence, species_id, species, and for fusion clip_start and clip_end. Optional filename for multi-file inputs. merge_method str / none Yes 'fusion' or 'reconstruct'. song_gap_threshold float / none Yes reconstruct only. Max gap in seconds. freq_iou_threshold float / None No reconstruct only. Frequency IoU gate. phrase_gap float / None No Fusion only. Join same-band boxes closer than this into phrase boxes. None or 0 keeps call-level boxes. This function has no model default. resolve_merge_settings fills it in. file_end float, Dict[str, float] or None No Fusion only. End of each file's last window. file_ends_from_raw builds the per-file dict from the unfiltered raw list, which keeps ownership identical to live detection. label_conf float / None No Birds-With-Labels only. Species score a box needs to be named after its top species. None uses 0.25.

resolve_merge_settings(model_config, song_gap, freq_iou, merge_method, phrase_gap) returns these keyword arguments from a raw JSON's model_config. Explicit arguments win, then the JSON, then the model defaults (window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap).

Returns: List[Dict]. The merged detections, with the fields below.

Field Type Description species str eBird species code, or bird species_id int Model class ID time_start float Start time in seconds time_end float End time in seconds avg_confidence float Average confidence of the merged raw boxes max_confidence float Highest confidence among the merged raw boxes detections_merged int Number of raw boxes that were merged freq_low_hz float Lower frequency edge in Hz freq_high_hz float Upper frequency edge in Hz filename str Source filename (multi-file inputs only)

Birds-With-Labels adds bird_id, species_confidence and alternatives. See Merged detection objects.

docs.title: The reconstruct_songs Function
docs.text:
The song merge on its own. merge_detections calls it for merge_method='reconstruct'. The default merge of both models is window fusion, so use merge_detections to merge saved raw detections as detection does.

from inference.detect_birds import reconstruct_songs

merged = reconstruct_songs(detections, song_gap_threshold)
merged = reconstruct_songs(detections, song_gap_threshold, freq_iou_threshold=0.6)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections List[Dict] / none Yes Raw detections, each with time_start, time_end, species_id, species, confidence, freq_low_hz, freq_high_hz. Optional filename key for multi-file inputs. song_gap_threshold float / none Yes Max gap in seconds between two detections of the same species to merge them into one song box. freq_iou_threshold float / None No If set, also require this frequency IoU. None keeps the time-only merger. With Just-Bird, merge_detections passes 0.6 unless overridden.

Returns: List[Dict]. The song boxes, sorted by (filename, time_start), with the same fields as merge_detections.

docs.title: The find_audio_files Function
docs.text:
Find all supported audio files in a path.

from inference.detect_birds import find_audio_files

paths = find_audio_files(audio_path)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description audio_path str / none Yes Path to a single audio file or a directory. Directories are searched recursively. verbose bool / True No If True, print how many audio files were found in a directory.

Returns: List[str]. A sorted list of file paths, relative if audio_path is relative. Supported extensions are .wav, .flac, .ogg and .mp3, in any letter case.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The examples use Just-Bird, the recommended model. It detects bird vocalizations with a single bird class. For species-level output, use the Birds-With-Labels model with its species mapping, as in the directory batch example.

docs.title: Basic Detection
docs.text:
Single fileDirectory batch 
from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Just-Bird",
)  # conf_threshold defaults to 0.15 for Just-Bird

detections = detector.detect(
    "recording.wav",
    output_path="results",
    output_formats=["simplified-csv"],
)

print(f"Found {len(detections)} detections")

from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Birds-With-Labels",
)  # conf_threshold defaults to 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels

detections = detector.detect(
    "/path/to/audio/folder",
    output_path="results",
    output_formats=["all"],
)

docs.title: Merging Saved Raw Detections
docs.text:
import json
from inference.detect_birds import file_ends_from_raw, merge_detections, resolve_merge_settings

with open("results/raw_detections.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

raw = data["detections"]
settings = resolve_merge_settings(data["model_config"])
kept = [d for d in raw if d["confidence"] >= 0.15]

merged = merge_detections(kept, **settings, file_end=file_ends_from_raw(raw))
print(f"{len(kept)} raw detections -> {len(merged)} merged detections")

docs.title: Parallel Inference
docs.text:
from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Just-Bird",
    num_workers=4,
)

detections = detector.detect(
    "long_recording.wav",
    output_path="results",
    output_formats=["simplified-csv"],
)

Lossy Audio Formats

MP3 and OGG compression can hide faint calls and high frequencies, so detection may get worse. In a study of avian recordings, MP3 compression reduced the detections of human listeners and automated recognisers [22]. Use WAV or FLAC whenever possible. If you must use MP3, use a bitrate of at least 256 kbps.

docs.title: References
docs.text: [22] MacPhail, A. G., Yip, D. A., Knight, E. C., Hedley, R., Knaggs, M., Shonfield, J., Upham-Mills, E., & Bayne, E. M. (2024). "Audio data compression affects acoustic indices and reduces detections of birds by human listening and automated recognisers." Bioacoustics, 33(1):74–90.

docs.title: F-Beta Score Analysis
docs.text: Sweep a range of confidence thresholds on raw (unmerged) detections and compute precision, recall, and F-beta scores for every species class at every threshold. The class returns DataFrames. It writes files only through plot_f_beta_curves, or when you save the DataFrames yourself.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
FBetaScoreAnalyzer(
    iou_threshold=0.25,
    beta=1.0,
    use_optimal_matching=True,
    song_gap=None,
    single_cls=False,
    single_cls_name="bird",
    freq_iou_threshold=None,
    log_initialization=True,
    merge_method=None,
    phrase_gap=None,
)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description iou_threshold float / 0.25 No IoU threshold for matching a detection to a ground truth label (0.0 to 1.0). Use the same value later in ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer for consistent evaluation. beta float / 1.0 No Beta parameter for the F-beta score. Controls the weighting of precision and recall. See Choosing beta below. use_optimal_matching bool / True No If True, uses the Hungarian algorithm for globally optimal assignment. If False, uses greedy matching. Greedy matching is faster on very large datasets but order-dependent and not recommended for published metrics. song_gap float / None No reconstruct merge only. Max gap in seconds to merge detections into song boxes at each threshold. When None, reads model_config.song_gap_threshold from the JSON, falling back to 0.1. single_cls bool / False No Collapse all species into one class for binary bird-detection evaluation. Use it for Just-Bird. single_cls_name str / 'bird' No Class name to use when single_cls=True. freq_iou_threshold float / None No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only. Frequency IoU gate. None uses the JSON value or 0.6. log_initialization bool / True No If True, print the settings when the analyzer is created. merge_method str / None No 'fusion' or 'reconstruct'. None uses model_config.merge_method from the JSON, which is 'fusion' for both models. phrase_gap float / None No Fusion only. None uses model_config.phrase_gap from the JSON, else the model default of 0.05 s.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description analyze_confidence_thresholds(detections_path, labels_path, confidence_thresholds, num_workers=1, detections_data=None, labels=None) pd.DataFrame Run the full threshold sweep. Primary entry point. find_optimal_thresholds(df) pd.DataFrame Best threshold per species from the sweep results. plot_f_beta_curves(df, output_dir, top_classes=10) None Write the curve plots and the heatmap to output_dir, which must exist. print_summary(df) None Print the best micro and macro scores and the top species. load_detections(detections_path) Dict Load raw detections JSON. load_labels(labels_path) List[Dict] Load ground truth labels CSV. filter_detections_by_confidence(detections_data, conf_threshold, verbose=False) List[Dict] Filter and merge detections at a single threshold.

docs.title: The analyze_confidence_thresholds Method
docs.text:
results_df = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path,
    labels_path,
    confidence_thresholds,
    num_workers=1,
    detections_data=None,
    labels=None,
)

Run the confidence-threshold sweep. At each threshold, raw detections are filtered by confidence and then merged. Then precision, recall, and F-beta scores are computed per species.

Input Must Be Raw (Unmerged) Detections

Pass the output of BirdCallDetector.detect(..., no_merge=True). Merged detections give wrong results, because the sweep filters and merges by itself at every threshold.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections_path str / none Yes Path to raw_detections.json from BirdCallDetector with no_merge=True. labels_path str / none Yes Path to the ground truth labels CSV file. confidence_thresholds List[float] / none Yes Ordered list of confidence thresholds to evaluate. Build it with np.round(np.arange(0.0, 1.01, 0.01), 2).tolist() for the default 101-step sweep. num_workers int / 1 No Number of worker processes. Each handles a disjoint subset of thresholds. detections_data dict / None No Preloaded raw-detections dict (same structure as load_detections). Skips re-reading the JSON when the same dump is scored more than once. labels list[dict] / None No Preloaded ground-truth rows (same structure as load_labels). Skips re-reading the CSV.

Returns: pd.DataFrame with one row per (species, confidence_threshold) combination, plus Overall_Micro and Overall_Macro summary rows per threshold. Columns: species, confidence_threshold, tp, fp, fn, precision, recall, f_beta_score.

docs.title: The find_optimal_thresholds Method
docs.text:
optimal = analyzer.find_optimal_thresholds(results_df)

Return one row per species, plus Overall_Micro and Overall_Macro, at the threshold where it reaches its best F-beta score. The columns are the same as in the sweep results. See Reading optimal_thresholds.csv.

docs.title: The load_detections Method
docs.text:
data = analyzer.load_detections(detections_path)

Load a raw_detections.json file produced by BirdCallDetector(..., no_merge=True). Returns the full JSON as a dict, including model_config metadata.

docs.title: The load_labels Method
docs.text:
labels = analyzer.load_labels(labels_path)

Load a ground truth labels CSV. Returns a list of dicts with keys filename, start_time, end_time, freq_low, freq_high, species. Label dicts use different key names than detection dicts. Anything passed via the labels= parameter of analyze_confidence_thresholds() must use these keys, or matching fails with a KeyError.

docs.title: The filter_detections_by_confidence Method
docs.text:
merged = analyzer.filter_detections_by_confidence(detections_data, conf_threshold, verbose=False)

Apply a single confidence threshold to raw detections, then merge the surviving boxes with the analyzer's merge settings. Used internally by analyze_confidence_thresholds() but also callable directly.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description detections_data Dict / none Yes Dict returned by load_detections(). conf_threshold float / none Yes Confidence threshold to apply. verbose bool / False No If True, print the filter details.

Returns: List[Dict]. The merged detections that survive the threshold.

docs.title: Choosing Beta
docs.text:
The beta parameter weights recall relative to precision in the F-beta formula [25], [27]:

\[ F_\beta = \frac{(1 + \beta^2) \cdot \text{precision} \cdot \text{recall}}{\beta^2 \cdot \text{precision} + \text{recall}} \] beta Score name Emphasis Recommended when 0.5 F0.5 Precision counts more than recall False positives are very costly 1.0 (default) F1 Equal weight General evaluation baseline 2.0 F2 Recall counts more than precision Missing a bird is worse than a false alarm

F1 or F2

The pipeline scripts and the models' default thresholds use F1. If missing a bird is worse than a false alarm in your project, use F2 (beta=2.0). It penalizes missed calls more than false detections.

docs.title: Building the Sweep Range
docs.text:
Use numpy.arange to generate the threshold list. Rounding keeps the thresholds readable in the results:

import numpy as np

# Default sweep: 101 thresholds from 0.00 to 1.00
thresholds = np.round(np.arange(0.00, 1.01, 0.01), 3).tolist()

# Coarse sweep: 19 thresholds (faster)
thresholds = np.round(np.arange(0.05, 1.00, 0.05), 3).tolist()

# Fine sweep around a known region
thresholds = np.round(np.arange(0.20, 0.50, 0.005), 3).tolist()

Runtime grows with the number of thresholds.

docs.title: Optimal Matching
docs.text:
By default, the Hungarian algorithm [15] finds the globally optimal assignment of detections to labels at each threshold. This is order-independent and fully reproducible.

Setting use_optimal_matching=False switches to greedy matching (first-come, first-served), which is faster for very large datasets but produces order-dependent results.

Not Recommended

Only use use_optimal_matching=False if runtime is critical and you understand the trade-offs. Always use the default for final published metrics.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
analyze_confidence_thresholds() and find_optimal_thresholds() return DataFrames and write nothing. Save them with DataFrame.to_csv, and call plot_f_beta_curves(df, output_dir) for the plots. The CLI script f_beta_score_analysis.py writes all of the files below. The filenames embed the beta value (e.g. f1.0_score_analysis.csv).

File Description f{beta}_score_analysis.csv Full results table: one row per (species, threshold). f{beta}_score_analysis.json Same data in JSON format. optimal_thresholds.csv Best threshold per species (maximising F-beta). Written from find_optimal_thresholds(). overall_micro_f{beta}_curve.png F-beta, precision, recall for micro-average across all species. overall_macro_f{beta}_curve.png F-beta, precision, recall for macro-average across all species. micro_vs_macro_f{beta}_comparison.png Side-by-side micro vs macro comparison. top_species_f{beta}_curves.png Per-species curves for the top performing species (top_classes, 12 in the CLI). all_species_f{beta}_curves.png Per-species curves for all species. f{beta}_score_heatmap.png Heatmap of F-beta per species (rows) vs threshold (columns). Species are sorted by their best F-beta. Gray cells mean the species has no labels and no detections at that threshold. args.yaml Every CLI argument used for this run. Written by the CLI script only.

docs.title: Reading optimal_thresholds.csv
docs.text:
find_optimal_thresholds() keeps the full result row at each species' best threshold:

species,confidence_threshold,tp,fp,fn,precision,recall,f_beta_score
amerob,0.35,42.0,6.0,8.0,0.8750,0.8400,0.8571
herthr,0.28,30.0,10.0,5.0,0.7500,0.8571,0.8000
Overall_Micro,0.33,72.0,16.0,13.0,0.8182,0.8471,0.8324
Overall_Macro,0.30,,,,0.8125,0.8486,0.8286

Use the Overall_Micro row to pick a single system-wide threshold when per-species thresholds are impractical.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The examples evaluate Just-Bird, so they pass single_cls=True. For Birds-With-Labels, drop it.

docs.title: Default F1 Sweep
docs.text:
import os

import numpy as np
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer

analyzer = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(beta=1.0, iou_threshold=0.25, single_cls=True)

thresholds = np.round(np.arange(0.00, 1.01, 0.01), 2).tolist()

results = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="data/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=thresholds,
)

optimal = analyzer.find_optimal_thresholds(results)
best = optimal.loc[optimal["species"] == "Overall_Micro"].iloc[0]
print(f"Best system-wide threshold: {best['confidence_threshold']:.2f} (F1 {best['f_beta_score']:.3f})")

# Optional: save the tables and plots
os.makedirs("results/f_beta_score_analysis", exist_ok=True)
results.to_csv("results/f_beta_score_analysis/f1.0_score_analysis.csv", index=False)
optimal.to_csv("results/f_beta_score_analysis/optimal_thresholds.csv", index=False)
analyzer.plot_f_beta_curves(results, "results/f_beta_score_analysis")

docs.title: F2 Sweep (Recall-Focused)
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer

analyzer = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(
    beta=2.0,
    iou_threshold=0.5,
    single_cls=True,
)

results = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="data/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=np.round(np.arange(0.00, 1.01, 0.01), 2).tolist(),
)

docs.title: Parallel Sweep (Fast)
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer

analyzer = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(single_cls=True)

results = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="data/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=np.round(np.arange(0.00, 1.01, 0.01), 2).tolist(),
    num_workers=8,
)

docs.title: Coarse Sweep, Then Fine Refinement
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer

analyzer = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(single_cls=True)

# Fast coarse pass
coarse = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="data/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=np.round(np.arange(0.05, 0.95, 0.05), 3).tolist(),
)

best = coarse[coarse["species"] == "Overall_Micro"]
peak = best.loc[best["f_beta_score"].idxmax(), "confidence_threshold"]

# Fine refinement around the peak
fine = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="data/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=np.round(np.arange(max(0, peak - 0.1), min(1, peak + 0.1), 0.005), 3).tolist(),
)

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This class sits at Step 2 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  BirdCallDetector(conf_threshold=0.001).detect(..., no_merge=True)      ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  FBetaScoreAnalyzer().analyze_confidence_thresholds(...)                 ->  results DataFrame
        FBetaScoreAnalyzer().find_optimal_thresholds(results)                   ->  best thresholds
Step 3  DetectionFilter().filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=best_conf)     ->  merged detections
        DetectionFilter().save_results(data, merged, output_path, best_conf, None)  ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer().analyze(..., output_path=...)                 ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

After running the sweep:

  1. Read the Overall_Micro row of find_optimal_thresholds() to get the best system-wide threshold.
  2. Pass that threshold to DetectionFilter.filter_detections() and save the result with save_results().
  3. Feed the resulting simplified.csv to ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer for species-level error analysis.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
[15] Kuhn, H. W. (1955). "The Hungarian method for the assignment problem." Naval Research Logistics Quarterly, 2(1–2):83–97.

[25] Powers, D. M. (2020). "Evaluation: from precision, recall and F-measure to ROC, informedness, markedness and correlation." arXiv preprint arXiv:2010.16061.

[27] van Rijsbergen, C. J. (1979). Information Retrieval (2nd ed.). Butterworths, London.

docs.title: Filter and Merge Detections
docs.text: Filter raw bird call detections by confidence and merge them, without re-running inference. DetectionFilter is the companion to BirdCallDetector(..., no_merge=True). It lets you try different thresholds in seconds on the same raw detection file.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
DetectionFilter(use_max_confidence=True)
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description use_max_confidence bool / True No Kept for API compatibility with FBetaScoreAnalyzer. Has no effect on raw-detection filtering, which always uses the per-clip confidence field.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Returns Description load_detections(input_path) Dict Load raw_detections.json. filter_detections(data, conf_threshold, song_gap, freq_iou_threshold, merge_method, phrase_gap) List[Dict] Filter by confidence, then merge. Primary entry point. save_results(data, filtered_detections, output_path, conf_threshold, song_gap, output_formats, merge_settings) None Write filtered results in one or more formats. save_filtered_json(data, filtered_detections, output_path, conf_threshold, song_gap, merge_settings) None Write JSON with algorithm metadata. save_filtered_csv(filtered_detections, output_path) None Write simplified CSV. save_filtered_xc_json(data, filtered_detections, output_path) None Write Xeno-Canto Annota-JSON. save_filtered_raven_txt(filtered_detections, output_path, multi_file=None) None Write a Raven Selection Table to output_path, or for a multi-file run one table per recording into raven/ next to it. multi_file=None treats the run as multi-file when any detection carries a filename.

docs.title: The load_detections Method
docs.text:
data = df.load_detections(input_path)

Load a raw_detections.json file produced by BirdCallDetector with no_merge=True.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description input_path str / none Yes Path to the raw detections JSON file. Only the CLI resolves a results/ directory to raw_detections.json and follows results/.active_run. Passing a directory here raises IsADirectoryError.

Returns: Dict with keys detections (list of raw clip dicts), model_config, and metadata fields.

docs.title: The filter_detections Method
docs.text:
merged = df.filter_detections(
    data,
    conf_threshold,
    song_gap=None,
    freq_iou_threshold=None,
    merge_method=None,
    phrase_gap=None,
)

Apply a confidence threshold to raw detections, then merge the surviving boxes with merge_detections. Unset merge settings come from the JSON's model_config, so the merge is the same as in the detection run. For both models that is window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description data Dict / none Yes Dict returned by load_detections(). conf_threshold float / none Yes Confidence threshold (0.0 to 1.0). All detections with confidence < threshold are discarded before merging. song_gap float / None No reconstruct merge only. Max gap in seconds between two detections of the same species to merge into one song. None reads model_config.song_gap_threshold, falling back to 0.1. freq_iou_threshold float / None No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only. Frequency IoU gate. None uses the JSON value or 0.6. merge_method str / None No 'fusion' or 'reconstruct'. None reads model_config.merge_method, which is 'fusion' for both models. phrase_gap float / None No Fusion only. Join same-band boxes closer than this many seconds. None reads model_config.phrase_gap, else 0.05 s.

Returns: List[Dict]. The merged detections. For single-file input each one gets the recording's filename.

Why filter raw clips and not merged boxes?

BirdCallDetector also filters first and merges afterwards. Filtering merged boxes by their average or maximum confidence gives different and generally worse results.

docs.title: The save_results Method
docs.text:
df.save_results(
    data,
    filtered_detections,
    output_path,
    conf_threshold,
    song_gap,
    output_formats=None,
    merge_settings=None,
)

Write filtered detections to one or more output formats under output_path.

Parameter Type / Default Required? Description data Dict / none Yes Original data dict from load_detections(). Used to preserve model_config in JSON output. filtered_detections List[Dict] / none Yes Merged detections returned by filter_detections(). output_path str / none Yes Output directory. It is created if it does not exist. conf_threshold float / none Yes Threshold applied. Recorded in filtering_config of the JSON output. song_gap float or None / none Yes Song gap recorded in filtering_config. Pass None for window fusion. output_formats List[str] / ['json-with-algorithm-metadata', 'simplified-csv'] No One or more format keys: json-with-algorithm-metadata, simplified-csv, xeno-canto-annota-json, raven-selection-table, or all. merge_settings Dict / None No Merge settings to record in filtering_config, such as the output of resolve_merge_settings(). Without it, the JSON records only the threshold and the song gap.

docs.title: Confidence Threshold
docs.text: The threshold is applied to the raw per-clip detections before merging. So it means the same as the conf_threshold you would pass to BirdCallDetector.

docs.title: Merge Settings
docs.text:
Leave the merge settings at None to reuse the values from the JSON's model_config. Then the merge matches the original detection run.

Arguments Effect none (recommended) Window fusion with the phrase gap from the JSON (0.05 s) phrase_gap=0 One box per call or syllable phrase_gap=0.3 Longer phrase boxes merge_method='reconstruct', song_gap=0.2 Song merge. Wide song boxes joined across pauses up to 0.2 s.

song_gap alone has no effect, because the default merge is window fusion. See Merge Method.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
Files written by save_results() to output_path:

output_path/with_algorithm_metadata.json   <- json-with-algorithm-metadata
output_path/simplified.csv                 <- simplified-csv
output_path/xeno-canto-annota.json         <- xeno-canto-annota-json
output_path/raven_selection_table.txt      <- raven-selection-table (single-file input)
output_path/raven/<Filename>.txt           <- raven-selection-table (multi-file input, one per recording)

For the schema of each format, see Detection Output Formats.

docs.title: Basic Filter and Merge
docs.text:
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter

df = DetectionFilter()
data = df.load_detections("results/raw_detections.json")

merged = df.filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=0.35)
print(f"Merged: {len(merged)} detections")

df.save_results(
    data,
    merged,
    output_path="results/filtered_0.35",
    conf_threshold=0.35,
    song_gap=None,
)

docs.text:
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter
from inference.detect_birds import resolve_merge_settings

df = DetectionFilter()
data = df.load_detections("results/raw_detections.json")
merged = df.filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=0.25, phrase_gap=0.1)
settings = resolve_merge_settings(data["model_config"], phrase_gap=0.1)

df.save_results(

    conf_threshold=0.25,
    song_gap=settings["song_gap_threshold"],

    merge_settings=settings,

docs.title: Rapid Threshold Comparison
docs.text:
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter

df = DetectionFilter()
data = df.load_detections("results/raw_detections.json")

for threshold in [0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50]:
    merged = df.filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=threshold)
    print(f"conf={threshold:.2f} -> {len(merged)} detections")

docs.title: Apply the Threshold From F-Beta Analysis
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter

optimal = pd.read_csv("results/f_beta_score_analysis/optimal_thresholds.csv")
best_threshold = float(optimal.loc[optimal["species"] == "Overall_Micro", "confidence_threshold"].iloc[0])

df = DetectionFilter()
data = df.load_detections("results/raw_detections.json")
merged = df.filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=best_threshold)

df.save_results(
    data,
    merged,
    output_path="results/final",
    conf_threshold=best_threshold,
    song_gap=None,
    output_formats=["simplified-csv", "json-with-algorithm-metadata"],
)

The CSV comes from the CLI script f_beta_score_analysis.py. In Python, take the threshold from FBetaScoreAnalyzer.find_optimal_thresholds() instead.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This class sits at Step 3 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  BirdCallDetector(conf_threshold=0.001).detect(..., no_merge=True)      ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  FBetaScoreAnalyzer().analyze_confidence_thresholds(...)                 ->  results DataFrame
        FBetaScoreAnalyzer().find_optimal_thresholds(results)                   ->  best thresholds
Step 3  DetectionFilter().filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=best_conf)     ->  merged detections
        DetectionFilter().save_results(data, merged, output_path, best_conf, None)  ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer().analyze(..., output_path=...)                 ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

When to Use This Class

  • After F-beta analysis: Apply the best threshold without re-running inference.
  • For rapid threshold experiments: Test multiple thresholds on the same raw file in seconds.
  • To generate CSV files: Produce CSV files compatible with ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer or external tools.
  • For custom thresholds: Apply any threshold outside your original sweep range.

docs.title: Typical Workflows
docs.text:
This chapter shows how to assemble the API classes into end-to-end Python scripts. For a description of every parameter, see the dedicated API pages. For the equivalent CLI commands, see CLI Workflows.

For the data formats of detections and ground truth annotations, see Data In/Out.

The examples run from the project root with src/ on the import path. See Setup.

docs.title: Simple Workflow for Detection Only
docs.text: Run inference on a single file or a directory of audio files. Both examples rely on the defaults for all other parameters. The confidence threshold defaults to the model's value (0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels).

docs.title: Single File
docs.text:
from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Just-Bird",
)

detections = detector.detect(
    "path/to/recording.wav",
    output_path="results",
)
# Writes: results/with_algorithm_metadata.json

docs.title: Directory Batch
docs.text:
from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector

detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Birds-With-Labels",
)

detections = detector.detect(
    "path/to/audio/folder",
    output_path="results",
    output_formats=["simplified-csv"],
)
# Writes: results/simplified.csv

Species Mapping Values

species_mapping is "Just-Bird" or "Birds-With-Labels" and must match the model. See Audio and Model Inputs: Species mapping. config.get_species_mapping_for_model(model_path) infers it from the model filename.

docs.title: Simple Workflow for Detection and Evaluation
docs.text:
The following code runs inference and evaluates the results against ground truth annotations. Steps 2 to 4 build on the output of step 1. The example uses Just-Bird, so steps 2 and 4 pass single_cls=True. For Birds-With-Labels, change the model and mapping and drop single_cls=True.

Why run detection at low confidence?

FBetaScoreAnalyzer filters and merges the raw detections by itself at each threshold. Merged or already filtered detections would give wrong scores. Always run step 1 with conf_threshold=0.001 and no_merge=True.

import numpy as np
from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter
from evaluation.confusion_matrix_analysis import ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer

# Step 1: Run inference at very low confidence, keep raw detections
detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt",
    species_mapping="Just-Bird",
    conf_threshold=0.001,
)
detector.detect(
    "path/to/audio/folder",
    output_path="results",
    no_merge=True,
)
# Writes: results/raw_detections.json

# Step 2: Sweep confidence thresholds to find the best one
analyzer = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(single_cls=True)
results = analyzer.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path="results/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path="path/to/annotations.csv",
    confidence_thresholds=np.round(np.arange(0.0, 1.01, 0.01), 2).tolist(),
)
optimal = analyzer.find_optimal_thresholds(results)
best_conf = float(optimal.loc[optimal["species"] == "Overall_Micro", "confidence_threshold"].iloc[0])
# Returns DataFrames only. Nothing is written in this step.

# Step 3: Filter at the best threshold and merge
df = DetectionFilter()
data = df.load_detections("results/raw_detections.json")
merged = df.filter_detections(data, conf_threshold=best_conf)
df.save_results(data, merged, "results/filtered", best_conf, song_gap=None)
# Writes: results/filtered/with_algorithm_metadata.json and results/filtered/simplified.csv

# Step 4: Compute the confusion matrix
cm_analyzer = ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer(iou_threshold=0.25, single_cls=True)
matrix, species = cm_analyzer.analyze(
    detections_path="results/filtered/simplified.csv",
    labels_path="path/to/annotations.csv",
    output_path="results/confusion_matrix_analysis",
)
# Writes: results/confusion_matrix_analysis/confusion_matrix.csv, *.png, metadata.txt

Unlike the CLI, the API takes exact file paths. It does not follow results/.active_run.

docs.title: Complete Workflow Script
docs.text:
The following script mirrors the pipeline from CLI Workflows: Complete Workflow Script. Every parameter is set explicitly for full reproducibility.

import os

import numpy as np

from inference.detect_birds import BirdCallDetector, resolve_merge_settings
from evaluation.f_beta_score_analysis import FBetaScoreAnalyzer
from evaluation.filter_and_merge_detections import DetectionFilter
from evaluation.confusion_matrix_analysis import ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer

# Configuration
MODEL_PATH          = "models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
SPECIES_MAPPING     = "Just-Bird"
SINGLE_CLS          = True         # True for Just-Bird, False for Birds-With-Labels
AUDIO_PATH          = "data/audio/"
LABELS_PATH         = "data/annotations.csv"
RESULTS_DIR         = "results"

CONF_LOW            = 0.001        # Step 1: capture all raw detections
BETA                = 1.0          # Step 2: F1, as in the pipeline scripts
CONF_RANGE_MIN      = 0.00
CONF_RANGE_MAX      = 1.00
CONF_RANGE_STEP     = 0.01
IOU_THRESHOLD       = 0.25         # Steps 2 and 4: matching strictness
PHRASE_GAP          = 0.05         # Steps 2 and 3: window fusion phrase gap (seconds)
NMS_IOU             = 0.7          # Step 1: NMS inside each clip
NUM_WORKERS_DETECT  = 1
NUM_WORKERS_SWEEP   = 8
OUTPUT_FORMATS      = ["simplified-csv", "json-with-algorithm-metadata"]

# Step 1: Inference
print("=== Step 1: Inference ===")
detector = BirdCallDetector(
    model_path=MODEL_PATH,
    species_mapping=SPECIES_MAPPING,
    conf_threshold=CONF_LOW,
    nms_iou_threshold=NMS_IOU,
    phrase_gap=PHRASE_GAP,
    num_workers=NUM_WORKERS_DETECT,
)
detector.detect(
    audio_path=AUDIO_PATH,
    output_path=RESULTS_DIR,
    no_merge=True,
)

# Step 2: F-beta sweep
print("\n=== Step 2: F-beta score analysis ===")
sweep_output = f"{RESULTS_DIR}/f_beta_score_analysis"
os.makedirs(sweep_output, exist_ok=True)

fbeta = FBetaScoreAnalyzer(
    iou_threshold=IOU_THRESHOLD,
    beta=BETA,
    phrase_gap=PHRASE_GAP,
    single_cls=SINGLE_CLS,
)
thresholds = np.round(
    np.arange(CONF_RANGE_MIN, CONF_RANGE_MAX + CONF_RANGE_STEP / 2, CONF_RANGE_STEP), 3
).tolist()
results_df = fbeta.analyze_confidence_thresholds(
    detections_path=f"{RESULTS_DIR}/raw_detections.json",
    labels_path=LABELS_PATH,
    confidence_thresholds=thresholds,
    num_workers=NUM_WORKERS_SWEEP,
)
optimal = fbeta.find_optimal_thresholds(results_df)
results_df.to_csv(f"{sweep_output}/f{BETA}_score_analysis.csv", index=False)
optimal.to_csv(f"{sweep_output}/optimal_thresholds.csv", index=False)
fbeta.plot_f_beta_curves(results_df, sweep_output)

best_conf = float(optimal.loc[optimal["species"] == "Overall_Micro", "confidence_threshold"].iloc[0])
print(f"\nBest threshold (micro-average): {best_conf:.2f}")

# Step 3: Filter and merge
print("\n=== Step 3: Filter and merge ===")
merge_output = f"{RESULTS_DIR}/filtered_{best_conf:.2f}"

df_filter = DetectionFilter()
raw_data = df_filter.load_detections(f"{RESULTS_DIR}/raw_detections.json")
merged = df_filter.filter_detections(raw_data, conf_threshold=best_conf, phrase_gap=PHRASE_GAP)
merge_settings = resolve_merge_settings(raw_data["model_config"], phrase_gap=PHRASE_GAP)
df_filter.save_results(
    raw_data,
    merged,
    output_path=merge_output,
    conf_threshold=best_conf,
    song_gap=merge_settings["song_gap_threshold"],
    output_formats=OUTPUT_FORMATS,
    merge_settings=merge_settings,  # recorded in filtering_config of the JSON
)
print(f"Kept {len(merged)} merged detections at conf >= {best_conf:.2f}")

# Step 4: Confusion matrix
print("\n=== Step 4: Confusion matrix ===")
cm_analyzer = ConfusionMatrixAnalyzer(
    iou_threshold=IOU_THRESHOLD,
    use_2d_iou=True,
    include_background=True,
    single_cls=SINGLE_CLS,
)
matrix, species = cm_analyzer.analyze(
    detections_path=f"{merge_output}/simplified.csv",
    labels_path=LABELS_PATH,
    output_path=f"{RESULTS_DIR}/confusion_matrix_analysis",
)

print(f"\nClasses evaluated: {[s for s in species if s != 'background']}")
print("Done. Results written to:", RESULTS_DIR)

docs.title: Confusion Matrix Analysis
docs.text: Compute a confusion matrix comparing filtered detection results against ground truth labels. Matches detections to labels using IoU with the Hungarian (optimal) algorithm, then builds a per-species confusion matrix showing correct classifications, misclassifications, false positives, and false negatives.

docs.title: Usage Synopsis
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py \
    --detections results \
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv

python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py `
    --detections results `
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv

python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py ^
    --detections results ^
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --detections PATH / results No Detections CSV file or results/ directory from filter_and_merge_detections.py. Default resolves to simplified.csv (follows results/.active_run). --labels PATH / none Yes Path to the ground truth labels CSV file. Must use the same column format as the detections file. --iou-threshold FLOAT / 0.25 No IoU threshold for matching a detection to a ground truth label. A detection is a True Positive only if its IoU with a matched label meets or exceeds this value. --use-1d-iou flag / off No Use 1D IoU (time overlap only) instead of the default 2D IoU (time and frequency). Faster but less accurate. --no-background flag / off No Omit the background class from the confusion matrix. By default, unmatched detections and unmatched labels are recorded in a background row and column. --single-cls flag / off No Collapse all species into a single class for binary bird-detection evaluation. Use it for Just-Bird. --single-cls-name STR / bird No Class name to use when --single-cls is active. --output-path PATH / results/confusion_matrix_analysis No Output directory for all result files. Created automatically if it does not exist.

docs.title: IoU Matching Threshold
docs.text:
--iou-threshold determines how strictly a detection must overlap a ground truth label to count as a True Positive. The best value depends on how precisely your annotations define the temporal and spectral extent of each call.

Value Strictness Typical use 0.1 Very lenient Useful when annotations are coarse 0.25 (default) Moderate Good starting point for most datasets 0.5 Strict When annotations are precise and detailed

Matching Algorithm

The script always uses the Hungarian algorithm [15] (optimal matching). This means the globally best assignment of detections to labels is found regardless of their order in the file. Results are fully reproducible.

docs.title: 1D IoU vs 2D IoU
docs.text:
2D IoU (default) measures the overlap of the two time-frequency boxes. The intersection area is divided by the union area:

\[ \text{IoU}_{2D} = \frac{A_{\cap}}{A_1 + A_2 - A_{\cap}}, \qquad A_{\cap} = t_{\text{overlap}} \cdot f_{\text{overlap}} \]

Here \(A_1\) and \(A_2\) are the areas (duration × bandwidth) of the detection and the label.

1D IoU (--use-1d-iou) measures overlap in time only:

\[ \text{IoU}_{1D} = \frac{t_{\text{overlap}}}{t_{\text{union}}} \]

Which to use?

2D IoU is more accurate because it accounts for both when and at what frequency a call occurs. Use --use-1d-iou only if your frequency annotations are unreliable or absent.

docs.title: Background Class
docs.text:
By default, the confusion matrix includes a background class. Rows are the predicted class, columns are the true (annotated) class:

  • Background column (last column): detections that did not match any ground truth label. These are False Positives.
  • Background row (last row): ground truth labels that were not matched by any detection. These are False Negatives.

Use --no-background if you only want to see the species-level confusion (correct or wrong species label), without the FP and FN counts.

docs.title: Single-Class Mode
docs.text:
--single-cls remaps all species labels in both detections and ground truth to the same class name (default: bird). It evaluates whether the model finds bird calls at all, independent of species classification. Use it for Just-Bird, which has only the bird class.

The single-class matrix

With the background class, the matrix is 2×2. It holds the True Positives, the False Positives and the False Negatives. The background-background cell is always 0, because there are no true negatives in event detection:

Pred \ True bird background bird TP FP background FN 0

With --no-background, only the TP cell remains.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
All files are written to the --output-path directory.

FileDescription confusion_matrix.csv Raw confusion matrix as a CSV. confusion_matrix_detailed.csv Same matrix with labeled pred_<class> rows and true_<class> columns. confusion_matrix_normalized.png Heatmap visualization, column-normalized: each true-class column sums to 1, showing how that class's instances were distributed across predictions. confusion_matrix_raw.png Heatmap visualization showing raw counts. metadata.txt Analysis parameters, file paths, species list, and detection/label counts. args.yaml Every CLI argument used for this run, including defaults. Written so confusion-matrix runs can be compared later.

docs.title: Reading the Confusion Matrix
docs.text:
The matrix uses predicted class (rows) × true class (columns) convention.

\[ \begin{array}{r|cccc} \text{Pred} \setminus \text{True} & \text{amerob} & \text{herthr} & \text{yelwar} & \text{bg} \\ \hline \text{amerob} & \mathbf{45} & 2 & 1 & 3 \\ \text{herthr} & 3 & \mathbf{38} & 0 & 2 \\ \text{yelwar} & 1 & 0 & \mathbf{52} & 1 \\ \text{background} & 4 & 2 & 1 & \mathbf{0} \\ \end{array} \]

bg stands for the background row and column, the last one. It exists only without --no-background.

Cell Meaning Diagonal cell [i, i] True Positives for species i Off-diagonal cell [i, j] (i ≠ j) Species i detected but actually species j (misclassification) background column cell [i, bg] Detections of species i that did not match any ground truth label (False Positives) background row cell [bg, j] Ground truth labels for species j that had no matching detection (False Negatives)
