docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This script sits at Step 4 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  detect_birds.py --conf 0.001 --no-merge    ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  f_beta_score_analysis.py                   ->  f_beta_score_analysis/optimal_thresholds.csv
Step 3  filter_and_merge_detections.py --conf 0.15 ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  confusion_matrix_analysis.py               ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

Input File Format

Both --detections and --labels must use the six-column schema described in CSV schema on the Ground-Truth Labels page. Filenames are matched by stem only. For details, see Filename matching.

docs.title: References
docs.text: [15] Kuhn, H. W. (1955). "The Hungarian method for the assignment problem." Naval Research Logistics Quarterly, 2(1–2):83–97.

docs.title: Detecting Birds
docs.text: Detect bird calls in audio files of any length with a trained YOLO model. detect_birds.py processes WAV, FLAC, OGG, and MP3 files through the same log-floor spectrogram pipeline used during training. It returns time and frequency boxes with species labels and confidence scores.

docs.title: Usage Synopsis
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
python src/inference/detect_birds.py \
    --audio path/to/audio.wav \
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt \
    --species-mapping Just-Bird

python src/inference/detect_birds.py `
    --audio path/to/audio.wav `
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt `
    --species-mapping Just-Bird

python src/inference/detect_birds.py ^
    --audio path/to/audio.wav ^
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt ^
    --species-mapping Just-Bird

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --audio PATH / none Yes Path to an audio file (WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3) or a directory. Directories are searched recursively for all supported audio files. --model PATH / none Yes Path to the trained YOLO model file (.pt, .onnx or .tflite). --species-mapping CHOICE / none Yes Just-Bird or Birds-With-Labels, the model the class IDs come from. It maps them to eBird codes and sets the default threshold. Must match the model. See Species mapping in the Data section. --output-path PATH / results No Output directory for result files (default: results/, auto-versioned to results/run_N/ when outputs already exist). See Output Formats. --output-format CHOICE [...] / json-with-algorithm-metadata No One or more output formats (space-separated). Accepts json-with-algorithm-metadata, simplified-csv, xeno-canto-annota-json, raven-selection-table, or all. Ignored when --no-merge is set (only raw_detections.json is written). --conf FLOAT / model default No Confidence threshold (0.0–1.0). Detections below this value are discarded. The default is 0.15 for Just-Bird and 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels, for direct use. For evaluation workflows, use 0.001 together with --no-merge to retain all raw detections. --nms-iou FLOAT / 0.7 No IoU threshold for Non-Maximum Suppression inside each 3-second clip. Higher values keep more overlapping detections. Lower values suppress more aggressively. --merge CHOICE / auto No How detections from the 50%-overlap windows are merged: fusion (window ownership + weighted box fusion, tight call-level boxes), reconstruct (song merge with --song-gap and --freq-iou), or auto, which is fusion for both models. See Merging the Windows. --phrase-gap FLOAT / 0.05 No Fusion only. Join boxes in the same frequency band that are closer than this many seconds into one phrase box. 0 keeps one box per call or syllable. See Phrase Gap. --label-conf FLOAT / 0.25 No Birds-With-Labels only. A box is named after its top species when that species' score reaches this value, and bird otherwise. See Species Names. --song-gap FLOAT / 0.1 No reconstruct merge only. Maximum gap in seconds between two detections of the same species that are still merged into one song box. Increase for species with long pauses between phrases. Decrease to keep phrases separate. --freq-iou FLOAT / 0.6 for Just-Bird, off otherwise No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only. Minimum frequency IoU required before two bird detections are merged into one song. Birds-With-Labels ignores this flag and keeps the time-only merger. Pass a negative value to force the time-only merger for Just-Bird. --num-workers INT / 1 No Number of CPU processes for spectrogram features, rendering, and multi-file preprocess. YOLO inference stays in the parent and runs in batches. --no-merge flag / off No Evaluation mode: clip-level detections only, writes raw_detections.json and ignores --output-format. Use it with a low --conf (e.g. 0.001) for f_beta_score_analysis.py and filter_and_merge_detections.py. --verbose flag / off No Print per-file processing details, clip-level progress bars, and a detection summary. Default is a single file-level progress bar.

Environment must match the model format

An environment runs .pt models and the format it was installed for. Loading a .onnx or .tflite model without its runtime stops with an error that names the install command. Run python install.py --model-format <FORMAT> in a separate environment for each format you want to use. See Install Parameters for the full table.

docs.title: Confidence Threshold
docs.text:
The confidence threshold (--conf) is the single most important tuning parameter. It controls how many detections reach the output.

Use case Recommended value Quick field recording scan 0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels (default) High-precision output (few false positives) 0.4 to 0.6 Comprehensive evaluation (feed into F-beta sweep) 0.001 with --no-merge

Evaluation Workflow Tip

For evaluation, run detection once at a very low confidence (--conf 0.001 --no-merge) to capture all candidate detections as raw JSON. Then use f_beta_score_analysis.py to find the best threshold. Apply it with filter_and_merge_detections.py, which needs no new inference run.

docs.title: Merge Method
docs.text:
--merge picks how the detections of the overlapping windows become the final boxes.

Value Output fusion (default for both models) One tight box per call, or per phrase with --phrase-gap reconstruct Wide song boxes, joined with --song-gap

auto picks fusion. --song-gap and --freq-iou only apply to reconstruct, and --phrase-gap only to fusion. Merging the Windows explains both merges.

docs.title: Phrase Gap
docs.text:
With fusion, --phrase-gap joins boxes in the same frequency band that are less than this many seconds apart.

Value Effect 0 One box per call or syllable. Use this if your annotations box single calls. 0.05 (default) Joins only boxes that nearly touch, for recordings of any annotation convention. 0.1 to 0.5 Longer phrase boxes, if your annotations box phrases or songs.

Phrase Gap shows how the gap changes the scores.

docs.title: Song Gap Threshold
docs.text:
This applies only to the reconstruct merge (--merge reconstruct). With window fusion, the default, --song-gap has no effect. The song merge joins detections of the same species that follow each other in time into one song box. Two detections are merged when the gap between them is at most --song-gap seconds.

Raw detections (same species):
  71.80s - 72.11s
  72.50s - 73.20s   <- gap = 0.39 s  (merged if song-gap >= 0.39)
  73.50s - 75.24s   <- gap = 0.30 s  (merged if song-gap >= 0.30)

Result with --song-gap 0.5:
  71.80s - 75.24s   (3 detections merged, avg_confidence reported)
Value Effect 0.05 Very conservative. Only detections that nearly touch are merged. 0.1 (default) Good balance for most species 0.5 Moderate. Merges phrases separated by short pauses. 2.0 Aggressive. May merge distinct song bouts.

docs.title: Frequency IoU Gate for Just-Bird
docs.text:
This also applies only to --merge reconstruct. Just-Bird predicts a single class. Two songs that overlap in time would otherwise become one box, and the frequency span would grow to cover both. When --species-mapping is Just-Bird, a detection joins an open song only if the time gap is within --song-gap and the frequency IoU is at least --freq-iou (default 0.6). Several songs can stay open at once.

Birds-With-Labels does not use this gate. Different species already stay in separate groups.

docs.title: NMS IoU Threshold
docs.text:
--nms-iou is applied by YOLO inside each 3-second spectrogram clip. Of two boxes that overlap by more than this IoU, it keeps only the one with the higher confidence. Duplicates from overlapping windows are handled later by the merge.

Relationship to the merge

--nms-iou removes duplicates within each clip. The merge (window fusion, or --song-gap with reconstruct) then combines the detections of overlapping clips. They operate at different stages of the pipeline and do not conflict.

docs.title: Parallel Workers
docs.text:
With --num-workers, CPU work (spectrogram features, rendering, and whole-file preprocess on folders) runs in a process pool so each worker has its own GIL and a single BLAS thread. YOLO inference stays in the parent process and is batched, which avoids loading extra model copies and is safer on a single GPU. Matches the num_workers constructor argument.

Memory Usage

--num-workers does not load extra YOLO weights. Workers add RAM for matplotlib and librosa only. The parent holds one model (and one GPU context when using CUDA).

docs.title: Noise Floor
docs.text: Each clip's noise floor is taken over the 60 s of audio up to the clip's end (rolling floor), so nothing after a clip changes its boxes. The JSON output records the floor window in model_config.floor_window_seconds.

docs.title: Evaluation Mode
docs.text:
With --no-merge, detect_birds.py enters evaluation mode:

  • The merge is skipped, so the clip-level detections are kept.
  • Only raw_detections.json is written under --output-path (default results/).
  • --output-format is ignored. A note is printed if other formats were requested.

Use this for the detection and evaluation workflow. For normal field use, omit --no-merge and pick formats with --output-format.

docs.title: Choosing Output Formats
docs.text: --output-format accepts one or more format names separated by spaces. Specify all to write every format in one run. For full schema documentation of each format see Detection Output Formats.

docs.title: Species Mapping
docs.text: The --species-mapping name must match the label space the model was trained on. It is not inferred from the weights filename. You pass it explicitly. For details, see Species mapping in the Data section.

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
The --output-format flag controls which file(s) are written under --output-path (unless --no-merge is set). Full schema documentation for every format, including JSON field tables and CSV column definitions, is in Detection Output Formats.

Every run also writes args.yaml in the same output directory. That file records every CLI argument used for the run, including defaults, so you can compare settings such as --nms-iou and --phrase-gap across result folders.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The examples use Just-Bird, the recommended model. It detects bird vocalizations with a single bird class. For species-level output, use the Birds-With-Labels model with its species mapping, as in the verbose logging example.

docs.title: F-Beta Score Analysis
docs.text: Sweep a range of confidence thresholds on raw (unmerged) detections and compute precision, recall, and F-beta scores for every species class at every threshold. Generates performance curves, a species-vs-threshold heatmap, and an optimal_thresholds.csv table identifying the best operating point per species.

docs.title: Usage Synopsis
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py \
    --raw-detections results \
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv \
    --single-cls

python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py `
    --raw-detections results `
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv `
    --single-cls

python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py ^
    --raw-detections results ^
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv ^
    --single-cls

Input Must Be Raw (Unmerged) Detections

This script expects the JSON output of detect_birds.py --no-merge. At each threshold it filters the raw boxes first and merges the survivors afterwards, as detect_birds.py does. Passing merged detections gives wrong results.

The synopsis uses --single-cls for Just-Bird. Drop it for Birds-With-Labels to score each species.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --raw-detections PATH / results No Raw detections file or results/ directory from detect_birds.py --no-merge. Default resolves to raw_detections.json (follows results/.active_run when re-running). Must contain per-clip confidence scores. --labels PATH / none Yes Path to the ground truth labels CSV file. Filenames are matched without extensions. --conf-range MIN MAX STEP / 0.00 1.0 0.01 No Confidence threshold range to test. Three space-separated floats: minimum, maximum, and step size. The default tests 101 thresholds from 0.00 to 1.00 in steps of 0.01. --beta FLOAT / 1.0 No Beta parameter for the F-beta score formula. Controls the precision/recall trade-off. See choosing beta below. --iou-threshold FLOAT / 0.25 No IoU threshold for matching a detection to a ground truth label (0.0 to 1.0). --merge CHOICE / auto No fusion (window ownership + weighted box fusion) or reconstruct (song merge with --song-gap and --freq-iou). auto uses model_config.merge_method from the JSON, which is fusion for both models. See Window fusion. --phrase-gap FLOAT / from JSON or 0.05 No Fusion only. Join same-band boxes closer than this many seconds into one phrase box. 0 turns it off. Omit to use model_config.phrase_gap from the JSON, else the model default of 0.05 s. --song-gap FLOAT / from JSON or 0.1 No reconstruct merge only. Max gap in seconds for merging surviving detections into song boxes at each threshold. Defaults to model_config.song_gap_threshold from the JSON. --freq-iou FLOAT / 0.6 for Just-Bird, off otherwise No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only. Minimum frequency IoU required before two bird detections merge into one song at each threshold. Omit to use the JSON value or 0.6. Pass a negative value for the time-only merger. --single-cls flag / off No Collapse all species into one class for binary bird-detection evaluation. Use it for Just-Bird. --single-cls-name STR / bird No Class name to use when --single-cls is active. --no-optimal-matching flag / off No Use greedy matching instead of the Hungarian algorithm. Not recommended: greedy matching is order-dependent and produces suboptimal, less reproducible results. --no-plot flag / off No Skip generating plot files. Useful for fast sweeps in CI or scripted pipelines. --output-path PATH / results/f_beta_score_analysis No Output directory for all result files. Created automatically if it does not exist. --num-workers INT / 1 No Number of worker processes for parallelising the confidence-threshold sweep. Each worker handles a subset of thresholds independently.

docs.title: Choosing Beta
docs.text:
The beta parameter (--beta) weights recall relative to precision in the F-beta formula [25], [27]:

\[ F_\beta = \frac{(1 + \beta^2) \cdot \text{precision} \cdot \text{recall}}{\beta^2 \cdot \text{precision} + \text{recall}} \]

where

\[ \text{precision} = \frac{TP}{TP + FP} \qquad \text{recall} = \frac{TP}{TP + FN} \] Beta Score name Emphasis Recommended when 0.5 F0.5 Precision counts more than recall False positives are very costly 1.0 (default) F1 Equal weight General evaluation baseline 2.0 F2 Recall counts more than precision Missing a bird is worse than a false alarm

F1 or F2

The pipeline scripts and the models' default thresholds use F1. If missing a bird is worse than a false alarm in your project, use F2 (--beta 2.0). It penalizes missed calls more than false detections and usually picks a lower threshold.

docs.title: Confidence Range
docs.text:
--conf-range MIN MAX STEP defines the grid of confidence thresholds to evaluate. Finer steps give smoother curves and more precise best thresholds. Runtime grows with the number of thresholds.

Example Thresholds tested 0.00 1.0 0.01 (default) 101 0.05 0.95 0.05 19 0.10 0.90 0.01 81

Speed Tip

Use --num-workers to parallelise the sweep across CPU cores. Each worker handles a disjoint set of thresholds independently. Combine with --no-plot for the fastest possible sweep.

docs.title: Detection Matching
docs.text: --iou-threshold controls how strictly a detection must overlap a ground truth label to count as a True Positive. Each detection and each label counts as one event, as in the event-based metrics for sound event detection [24]. The same value used here should be used later in confusion_matrix_analysis.py for a consistent evaluation.

docs.title: Optimal Matching
docs.text:
By default, the Hungarian algorithm [15] is used to find the globally optimal assignment of detections to labels at each threshold. This is order-independent and reproducible. The --no-optimal-matching flag switches to greedy matching (first-come, first-served), which is faster for very large datasets but produces order-dependent, suboptimal results.

Not Recommended

Only use --no-optimal-matching if runtime is critical and you understand the trade-offs. For final published metrics, always use the default optimal matching.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
All files are written to --output-path. The beta value is embedded in filenames (e.g. f1.0_score_analysis.csv for the default --beta 1.0).

File Description f{beta}_score_analysis.csv Complete results table: one row per (species, confidence threshold) combination with TP, FP, FN, precision, recall, and F-beta score. f{beta}_score_analysis.json Same data in JSON format. optimal_thresholds.csv Best confidence threshold per species (maximising F-beta score). overall_micro_f{beta}_curve.png F-beta, precision, and recall curves for the micro-average across all species. overall_macro_f{beta}_curve.png F-beta, precision, and recall curves for the macro-average across all species. micro_vs_macro_f{beta}_comparison.png Side-by-side comparison of micro and macro averaging methods. top_species_f{beta}_curves.png Per-species curves for the top 12 performing species. all_species_f{beta}_curves.png Per-species curves for all species. f{beta}_score_heatmap.png Heatmap of F-beta score per species (rows) vs confidence threshold (columns). Species are sorted by their best F-beta. Gray cells mean the species has no labels and no detections at that threshold. args.yaml Every CLI argument used for this run, including defaults. Written so F-beta runs can be compared later.

docs.title: Micro vs Macro Average
docs.text:
Two summary rows are included in the results for each threshold:

Type of Average Method What it tells you Overall_Micro Sum all TP, FP, FN across species, then compute F-beta Overall model performance. Dominated by frequent species. Overall_Macro Compute F-beta per species, then average Per-class fairness. Gives equal weight to rare and common species.

Check both: a high micro score with a low macro score means the model performs well on common species but poorly on rare ones.

A species with errors but no true positive at a threshold (only missed calls, or only false detections) scores 0 for precision, recall and F-beta, as with scikit-learn's zero_division=0. It therefore pulls the macro average down instead of dropping out of it. Precision, recall and F-beta are only left empty (NaN) for a species with no labels and no detections at that threshold.

docs.title: Reading the Optimal Thresholds File
docs.text:
optimal_thresholds.csv lists, for each species, the full result row (same columns as f{beta}_score_analysis.csv) at the confidence threshold where that species achieves its best F-beta score:

species,confidence_threshold,tp,fp,fn,precision,recall,f_beta_score
amerob,0.35,42.0,6.0,8.0,0.8750,0.8400,0.8571
herthr,0.28,30.0,10.0,5.0,0.7500,0.8571,0.8000
yelwar,0.42,46.0,4.0,5.0,0.9200,0.9020,0.9109
Overall_Micro,0.33,118.0,20.0,18.0,0.8551,0.8676,0.8613
Overall_Macro,0.30,,,,0.8216,0.8540,0.8671

In the Overall_Macro row, precision, recall and F-beta are each averaged over species separately, so its F-beta is not computed from the precision and recall shown and can lie outside them. Its tp / fp / fn are empty, which is also why the counts in the other rows are written as decimals (42.0).

Use the Overall_Micro or Overall_Macro row to pick a single system-wide threshold when per-species thresholds are impractical.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This script sits at Step 2 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  detect_birds.py --conf 0.001 --no-merge    ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  f_beta_score_analysis.py                   ->  f_beta_score_analysis/optimal_thresholds.csv
Step 3  filter_and_merge_detections.py --conf 0.15 ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  confusion_matrix_analysis.py               ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

After running this script:

  1. Open optimal_thresholds.csv and read the Overall_Micro row to find the best system-wide threshold.
  2. Pass that threshold to filter_and_merge_detections.py --conf <threshold>.
  3. Feed the resulting CSV into confusion_matrix_analysis.py for species-level error analysis.

docs.title: Filter and Merge Detections
docs.text: Filter raw bird call detections by confidence and merge them, without re-running inference. This script is the companion to detect_birds.py --no-merge. It lets you try different confidence thresholds on the same raw detection file in seconds.

docs.title: Usage Synopsis
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py \
    --raw-detections results \
    --conf 0.15

python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py `
    --raw-detections results `
    --conf 0.15

python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py ^
    --raw-detections results ^
    --conf 0.15

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --raw-detections PATH / results No Raw detections file or results/ directory from detect_birds.py --no-merge. Default resolves to raw_detections.json (follows results/.active_run). --conf FLOAT / model default No Confidence threshold for filtering (0.0 to 1.0). All raw detections with confidence < threshold are discarded before merging. Omit to use the default for model_config.species_mapping: 0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels. --merge CHOICE / auto No fusion (window ownership + weighted box fusion) or reconstruct (song merge with --song-gap and --freq-iou). auto uses model_config.merge_method from the JSON, which is fusion for both models. See Window fusion. --phrase-gap FLOAT / from JSON or 0.05 No Fusion only. Join same-band boxes closer than this many seconds into one phrase box. 0 turns it off. Omit to use model_config.phrase_gap from the JSON, else the model default of 0.05 s. --song-gap FLOAT / from JSON or 0.1 No reconstruct merge only. Maximum gap in seconds between two detections of the same species that are still merged into one song box. Omit to use model_config.song_gap_threshold from the JSON, else 0.1. --freq-iou FLOAT / 0.6 for Just-Bird, off otherwise No reconstruct merge with Just-Bird only. Minimum frequency IoU required before two bird detections merge into one song. Omit to use model_config.freq_iou_threshold when present, otherwise 0.6. Pass a negative value for the time-only merger. --output-path PATH / results No Output directory for result files. Each format writes a fixed descriptive filename inside this directory (see Output Files). The directory is created automatically if it does not exist. --output-format CHOICE [...] / json-with-algorithm-metadata simplified-csv No One or more output formats (space-separated). Accepts json-with-algorithm-metadata, simplified-csv, xeno-canto-annota-json, raven-selection-table, or all.

docs.title: Confidence Threshold
docs.text:
The --conf threshold is applied to the raw per-clip detections before merging. So it means the same as the --conf value you would pass to detect_birds.py.

Why filter raw clips and not merged boxes?

detect_birds.py also filters first and merges afterwards. Filtering merged boxes by their average or maximum confidence gives different and generally worse results.

docs.title: Merge Settings
docs.text:
If you leave the merge flags unset, the script reuses the values from the JSON's model_config block, which detect_birds.py wrote. So detection and post-processing use the same merge. For both models that is window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap.

Flag Effect --phrase-gap 0 One box per call or syllable --phrase-gap 0.05 Default. Joins only boxes that nearly touch. --phrase-gap 0.3 Longer phrase boxes --merge reconstruct --song-gap 0.2 Song merge. Wide song boxes joined across pauses up to 0.2 s.

--song-gap alone has no effect, because the default merge is window fusion. See Merge Method.

docs.title: Choosing Output Formats
docs.text: --output-format accepts one or more format names separated by spaces. Specify all to write every format in one run. For full schema documentation of each format see Detection Output Formats.

When run with --output-path results/merged, the following files are written depending on --output-format:

results/merged/xeno-canto-annota.json         <- xeno-canto-annota-json
results/merged/raven_selection_table.txt      <- raven-selection-table (single-file input)
results/merged/raven/<Filename>.txt           <- raven-selection-table (multi-file input, one per recording)

For the structure of each output file see Detection Output Formats.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
This script sits at Step 3 of the standard evaluation pipeline:

Step 1  detect_birds.py --conf 0.001 --no-merge    ->  raw_detections.json
Step 2  f_beta_score_analysis.py                   ->  f_beta_score_analysis/optimal_thresholds.csv
Step 3  filter_and_merge_detections.py --conf 0.15 ->  simplified.csv
Step 4  confusion_matrix_analysis.py               ->  confusion_matrix_analysis/

When to Use This Tool

  • After F-beta analysis: Apply the best threshold found by f_beta_score_analysis.py without re-running inference.
  • For rapid threshold experiments: Test multiple thresholds on the same raw file in seconds.
  • To generate CSV files: Produce ground-truth-compatible CSV files for external evaluation tools or confusion_matrix_analysis.py.
  • For custom thresholds: Apply any threshold that falls outside your original --conf-range.

docs.title: Merge Hyperparameter Search
docs.text:
Optional grid search of the merge gap and, if you want, --nms-iou on a frozen checkpoint. Most users never need this. The defaults in run_pipeline.sh are the usual evaluation path.

Advanced / optional

Skip this page unless you are already evaluating against labeled audio and want to retune merge parameters. For detection and F-beta with stock settings, see Typical Workflows.

Each setting is scored with the same F-beta protocol as f_beta_score_analysis.py. Raw detections are filtered by confidence and merged. Then they are matched to annotations.csv with the Hungarian algorithm on 2D IoU. Confidence is swept at every grid point. The reported number is the best Overall_Micro F-beta.

The gap that is searched depends on the merge method. Both models merge with window fusion, so by default the search tries --phrase-gaps. With --merge reconstruct it tries --song-gaps instead.

Learning-rate and augmentation search lives in BirdBox-Train and is also optional. Do not mix the two. Freeze the merge settings while training, then run this search on the winning weights.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
run_hpo.sh at the repository root is the intended way to run this search. Edit the variables at the top and leave exactly one option enabled. It works like run_pipeline.sh but is not part of the default pipeline.

Option A (default, cheap) reuses one raw_detections.json and only sweeps the phrase gap. Option B (expensive) re-runs detect_birds.py --no-merge once per --nms-iou value, then sweeps the phrase gap on each dump. Detection dominates wall time. Use B only when you need to search NMS.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Advanced / optional: search merge hyperparameters (phrase_gap, nms_iou)
# on a frozen model. Everyday detect + evaluate is run_pipeline.sh
# (or .bat / .ps1). Skip unless you have labels and want to retune merge.

# Exit immediately if a command fails
set -e

# Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
# If .venv does not exist, the script uses the current Python on PATH.
if [ -f ".venv/bin/activate" ]; then
    echo "Activating .venv"
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source ".venv/bin/activate"
fi


#### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####
# DATASET_NAME="Birds-With-Labels_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Western-US"
# DATASET_NAME="Hawaii_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset-subset"
DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset"


#### raw detections for Option A: the OUTPUT_PATH of run_pipeline.sh #####
RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH="results/Just-Bird"
# RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH="results/Birds-With-Labels"


#### select model #####
MODEL_PATH="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
# MODEL_PATH="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt"


#### select the species mapping (according to dataset and model) #####
SPECIES_MAPPING="Just-Bird"
# SPECIES_MAPPING="Birds-With-Labels"


#### toggle single class mode (true for Just-Bird) #####
USE_SINGLE_CLS=true
# USE_SINGLE_CLS=false


#### select output path #####
OUTPUT_PATH="results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge"


#### merge-parameter grid #####
# Both models merge with window fusion, so the gap searched is phrase_gap.
PHRASE_GAPS=(0.0 0.025 0.05 0.1 0.2)
NMS_IOUS=(0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8)

IOU_THRESHOLD=0.25
BETA=1.0
DETECT_CONF=0.001
DETECT_WORKERS=18
FBETA_WORKERS=9


#########################################################################
# Choose exactly one of the two options below (they are alternatives,
# not sequential steps). Detect + single F-beta stay in run_pipeline.sh.
# Freeze these merge params while training (BirdBox-Train/run_hpo.sh).
#
# Runtime: Option A reuses one raw_detections.json (no new detect).
# Option B re-runs detect_birds --no-merge once per NMS_IOUS value,
# which dominates wall time. Prefer A unless you need to search nms_iou.
#########################################################################


SINGLE_CLS_FLAG=()
if [ "${USE_SINGLE_CLS}" = true ]; then
    SINGLE_CLS_FLAG+=(--single-cls)
fi


### only enable one of the two ###
# Option A (cheap): sweep phrase_gap only. Reuses the existing
# detect_birds --no-merge dump (RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH/raw_detections.json).
# Does not run detection again. nms_iou is whatever that dump was built with.
echo "Option A: sweeping phrase_gap on existing raw detections (no new detect)..."
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
    --raw-detections "${RAW_DETECTIONS_PATH}" \
    --labels "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --phrase-gaps "${PHRASE_GAPS[@]}" \
    --iou-threshold "${IOU_THRESHOLD}" \
    --beta "${BETA}" \
    --num-workers "${FBETA_WORKERS}" \
    --no-plot \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"

# Option B (expensive): sweep nms_iou and phrase_gap.
# nms_iou is applied inside YOLO, so detect_birds --no-merge runs once per
# NMS_IOUS value (len(NMS_IOUS) full inference passes), then phrase_gap is
# swept on each dump. Comment Option A if you enable this.
# echo "Option B: re-running detect once per nms_iou, then sweeping phrase_gap..."
# python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
#     --model "${MODEL_PATH}" \
#     --audio "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/soundscape_data" \
#     --species-mapping "${SPECIES_MAPPING}" \
#     --labels "datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv" \
#     --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
#     --nms-ious "${NMS_IOUS[@]}" \
#     --phrase-gaps "${PHRASE_GAPS[@]}" \
#     --detect-conf "${DETECT_CONF}" \
#     --detect-workers "${DETECT_WORKERS}" \
#     --iou-threshold "${IOU_THRESHOLD}" \
#     --beta "${BETA}" \
#     --num-workers "${FBETA_WORKERS}" \
#     --no-plot \
#     "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"
# ### only enable one of the two ###


echo
echo "All tasks completed!"
echo "Merge HPO summary is in ${OUTPUT_PATH}/summary.csv"

# Option A (cheap): phrase gap only, reuse an existing --no-merge dump (no new detect)
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py `
    --raw-detections results/Just-Bird `
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv `
    --output-path results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge `
    --phrase-gaps 0.0 0.025 0.05 0.1 0.2 `
    --num-workers 9 `
    --no-plot `
    --single-cls

rem Option A (cheap): phrase gap only, reuse an existing --no-merge dump (no new detect)
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py ^
    --raw-detections results/Just-Bird ^
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv ^
    --output-path results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge ^
    --phrase-gaps 0.0 0.025 0.05 0.1 0.2 ^
    --num-workers 9 ^
    --no-plot ^
    --single-cls

Checkpoint Must Be Frozen

This search does not train. It only changes how existing boxes are suppressed (--nms-iou) and merged (the gap). Pass the same .pt you would use in detect_birds.py.

docs.title: What Is Searched
docs.text:
Parameter When it is applied Needs a new detect pass? --phrase-gaps In F-beta, after filtering by confidence. Window fusion only (the default). No. One raw_detections.json is enough. --song-gaps In F-beta, after filtering by confidence. Only with --merge reconstruct. No. One raw_detections.json is enough. --nms-ious Inside YOLO during detect_birds.py --no-merge Yes. One raw dump per NMS value. Confidence Swept automatically at every grid point No

--iou-threshold (matching detections to labels) is not part of this grid. Keep it at the evaluation default (0.25) so scores stay comparable to run_pipeline.sh.

Detection is the expensive part

The gap is applied in F-beta on an existing dump, so many gap values are cheap. --nms-iou is applied inside YOLO, so each NMS value is a full inference pass over the test set. Option A in run_hpo.sh never re-detects. Option B runs detection once per --nms-ious value.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type / Default Required? Description --raw-detections PATH / none Yes, unless --nms-ious Existing raw detections file or results directory from detect_birds.py --no-merge. Used for a gap-only search. --labels PATH / none Yes Ground truth annotations.csv. Filenames are matched without extensions. --output-path PATH / results/hyperopt_merge No Root directory for per-setting F-beta runs and summary.csv. --merge CHOICE / auto No Merge method to score: auto, fusion or reconstruct. auto uses the method in the detections JSON, which is window fusion for both models. --phrase-gaps FLOAT [...] / 0.0 0.025 0.05 0.1 0.2 No Phrase gaps in seconds to try with window fusion. --song-gaps FLOAT [...] / 0.0 0.1 0.2 0.5 1.0 2.0 No Song gaps in seconds to try with --merge reconstruct. Ignored with fusion. --nms-ious FLOAT [...] / unset No If set, re-run detect --no-merge once per NMS IoU (the expensive path), then sweep the gap on each dump. Requires --model, --audio, and --species-mapping. Omit this to reuse one dump (Option A). --model PATH / none With --nms-ious Frozen YOLO checkpoint. --audio PATH / none With --nms-ious Audio file or directory (typically the test set soundscape_data/ folder). --species-mapping CHOICE / none With --nms-ious Just-Bird or Birds-With-Labels. Must match the model. See species mapping. --detect-conf FLOAT / 0.001 No Confidence used when re-running detect for --nms-ious. Keep it low so F-beta can sweep later. --detect-workers INT / 8 No CPU workers for those detect passes. --iou-threshold FLOAT / 0.25 No IoU for matching detections to labels. Use the same value as f_beta_score_analysis.py. --beta FLOAT / 1.0 No F-beta weighting. Same meaning as in F-beta analysis. --conf-range MIN MAX STEP / 0.00 1.0 0.01 No Confidence grid at each (nms_iou, gap) pair. --num-workers INT / 8 No Worker processes for each F-beta confidence sweep. --no-plot flag / off No Skip F-beta plots (faster; run_hpo.sh sets this). --single-cls flag / off No Collapse all species into one class. Use it for Just-Bird. --single-cls-name STR / bird No Class name when --single-cls is set.

docs.title: Phrase Gaps
docs.text:
--phrase-gaps lists the phrase gaps to try. Window fusion first joins the boxes of overlapping windows. Then it joins boxes in the same frequency band that are closer in time than the phrase gap. A gap of 0 keeps one box per call. Larger gaps give longer phrase boxes. See phrase gap for details.

The gap is applied inside F-beta, after filtering by confidence. That is the same filter-then-merge policy as f_beta_score_analysis.py --phrase-gap. Because merging happens after detection, one --no-merge dump is enough to try every gap.

docs.title: Song Gaps
docs.text: --song-gaps is used only with --merge reconstruct. The song merge joins boxes of the same species when the gap between them is at most this value. See song gap.

docs.title: NMS IoU Values
docs.text:
--nms-ious lists the NMS IoU values to try. NMS removes duplicate boxes at detection time, inside YOLO on each 3-second clip. Changing it changes which boxes are written to raw_detections.json, so the script calls detect_birds.py --no-merge once per value. That is the main compute cost of Option B. Four NMS values mean four full test set inference runs.

NMS and the merge are different stages

NMS removes overlapping boxes within a clip. The merge then joins the surviving boxes across clips and time. Searching both is a product grid (NMS values × gaps), and each cell still sweeps confidence.

docs.title: Training Search and This Search
docs.text:
Training hyperparameter search is a separate, optional tool in BirdBox-Train. It retrains YOLO (learning rate, mixup and more) and scores every trial with one fixed set of merge settings. So trials differ only by training recipe.

If you later copy a winning best.pt into models/, this page is where you can retune the merge settings on labeled audio. Neither search is required for ordinary detection or evaluation.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
All files are written under --output-path. Each grid cell gets its own folder, named after the NMS value and the gap:

results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge/
  summary.csv
  nms_0.70/phrase_gap_0.050/
    f1.0_score_analysis.csv
    optimal_thresholds.csv
    score.json
  nms_0.70/phrase_gap_0.100/
    ...

With --merge reconstruct the cell folders are named song_gap_<value>. When --nms-ious is set, each NMS value also stores its detection dump at nms_<value>/detect/raw_detections.json.

File Description summary.csv One row per (nms_iou, gap) with the merge method, the gap, the best micro F-beta, its confidence, precision, and recall. score.json Same numbers for that cell. f{beta}_score_analysis.csv Full F-beta table for that cell (same schema as the standalone F-beta script). optimal_thresholds.csv Best confidence per species at that merge setting.

Open summary.csv and take the row with the highest micro_f1. Then set --nms-iou and MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap ...) in run_pipeline.sh to those values for the final test evaluation.

docs.title: Phrase Gap Only (Option A, No New Detect)
docs.text:
Run detect_birds.py --no-merge once first (Step 1 in run_pipeline.sh). Then reuse that dump:

CommandExpected Output (excerpt) 
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
    --raw-detections results/Just-Bird \
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv \
    --output-path results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge \
    --phrase-gaps 0.0 0.025 0.05 0.1 0.2 \
    --num-workers 9 \
    --no-plot \
    --single-cls

=== nms_iou=0.70 fusion phrase_gap=0.0 ===
...
micro F1.0=0.xxxx  conf=0.xx  P=0.xxxx  R=0.xxxx
=== nms_iou=0.70 fusion phrase_gap=0.025 ===
...
Best: nms_iou=0.7 fusion phrase_gap=0.05 micro F1.0=0.xxxx conf=0.xx
Wrote results/Just-Bird/hyperopt_merge/summary.csv

This is the default option in run_hpo.sh. Wall time is F-beta only (one dump, many gaps).

docs.title: NMS IoU and Phrase Gap Together (Option B, Re-Detect per NMS)
docs.text:
Command 
python src/evaluation/hyperopt_merge.py \
    --model models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt \
    --audio datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/soundscape_data \
    --species-mapping Birds-With-Labels \
    --labels datasets/Northeastern-US_testset/annotations.csv \
    --output-path results/Birds-With-Labels/hyperopt_merge \
    --nms-ious 0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8 \
    --phrase-gaps 0.05 0.1 \
    --detect-workers 18 \
    --num-workers 9 \
    --no-plot

Uncomment Option B in run_hpo.sh for the same grid, and comment out Option A so only one search runs. Expect one full --no-merge detection pass per --nms-ious value.

docs.title: After the Search
docs.text:
The usual BirdBox path stays run_pipeline.sh. Use this page only if you want different merge values than the pipeline defaults.

Usual (most users)     run_pipeline.sh     detect + F-beta + confusion matrix
Optional (this page)   run_hpo.sh          pick phrase_gap (and nms_iou) on a frozen model
                       then run_pipeline.sh with those values
Optional (Train repo)  run_hpo.sh          search training hyperparameters

If you did run the search:

  1. Read summary.csv and pick the best nms_iou and gap.
  2. Set those values in run_pipeline.sh: --nms-iou for detection, and MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap ...) for steps 2 and 3.
  3. Run the usual evaluation steps on the test set.

docs.title: Typical Workflows
docs.text:
This chapter documents all user-facing parameters for the executable scripts. Most CLI parameters have defaults that work well in many cases. Sometimes it helps to tune them for your dataset.

For the data formats of detections and ground truth annotations, see Data In/Out.

docs.title: Simple Workflow for Detection Only
docs.text:
The detection script runs on a single audio file or on a whole directory. Both examples rely on the default values of the CLI parameters. For full control, see Complete Workflow Script.

The examples use Just-Bird. For Birds-With-Labels, pass --model models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt --species-mapping Birds-With-Labels.

Select the tab below that matches your operating system.

docs.title: Single File Processing
docs.text:
Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
python src/inference/detect_birds.py \
    --audio path/to/recording.wav \
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt \

python src/inference/detect_birds.py `
    --audio path/to/recording.wav `
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt `
    --species-mapping Just-Bird

python src/inference/detect_birds.py ^

docs.title: Simple Workflow for Detection and Evaluation
docs.text:
The following scripts run inference and evaluate the results against ground truth annotations. They rely on the default values of the CLI parameters. For full control, see Complete Workflow Script.

Run detection with --no-merge, before any merging. The F-beta analysis merges by itself. At each confidence threshold it filters the raw boxes first and merges the survivors afterwards.

Steps 2 to 4 use default paths under results/. Step 1 writes results/raw_detections.json, or results/run_N/raw_detections.json if results/ already has outputs. Later steps follow results/.active_run and find raw_detections.json and simplified.csv by themselves.

The example uses Just-Bird, so steps 2 and 4 pass --single-cls. For Birds-With-Labels, change the model and mapping in step 1 and drop --single-cls.

Step 3 filters at the model's default threshold (0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels). To use the best threshold from step 2 instead, pass it with --conf. Step 2 prints it as the best Overall_Micro threshold.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
# Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and --no-merge to get raw detections
python src/inference/detect_birds.py \
    --audio path/to/audio/folder \
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt \
    --species-mapping Just-Bird \
    --output-path results \
    --conf 0.001 \
    --no-merge

# Step 2: Analyze F-beta scores to find the best threshold
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py \
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv \
    --single-cls

# Step 3: Filter raw detections at the model's default threshold and merge
# (add --conf <threshold> to use the best threshold from step 2)
python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py

# Step 4: Generate the confusion matrix
python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py \
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv \
    --single-cls

# Step 5: Examine the results in the results/ directory

# Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and --no-merge to get raw detections
python src/inference/detect_birds.py `
    --audio path/to/audio/folder `
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt `
    --species-mapping Just-Bird `
    --output-path results `
    --conf 0.001 `
    --no-merge

# Step 2: Analyze F-beta scores to find the best threshold
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py `
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv `
    --single-cls

# Step 3: Filter raw detections at the model's default threshold and merge
# (add --conf <threshold> to use the best threshold from step 2)
python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py

# Step 4: Generate the confusion matrix
python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py `
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv `
    --single-cls

# Step 5: Examine the results in the results/ directory

rem Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and --no-merge to get raw detections
python src/inference/detect_birds.py ^
    --audio path/to/audio/folder ^
    --model models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt ^
    --species-mapping Just-Bird ^
    --output-path results ^
    --conf 0.001 ^
    --no-merge

rem Step 2: Analyze F-beta scores to find the best threshold
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py ^
    --labels path/to/annotations.csv ^

rem Step 3: Filter raw detections at the model's default threshold and merge

rem Step 4: Generate the confusion matrix

docs.title: Complete Workflow Script
docs.text:
The following scripts give the most control over BirdBox. They are the pipeline scripts at the repository root.

Adapt any parameter to your use case. Each Python script has its own page in this chapter that describes its CLI parameters.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell)Windows (CMD) 
#!/bin/bash
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Default BirdBox workflow: detect birds and evaluate against labels.
# Same as run_pipeline.bat / run_pipeline.ps1 (other shells).
# Skip run_hpo.sh unless you need the advanced merge-parameter search.

# Exit immediately if a command fails
set -e

# Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
# If .venv does not exist, the script uses the current Python on PATH.
if [ -f ".venv/bin/activate" ]; then
    echo "Activating .venv"
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source ".venv/bin/activate"
fi


#### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####
# Just-Bird trained on the train and test splits of every regional dataset,
# so its scores on these test sets are in-domain.
# DATASET_NAME="Birds-With-Labels_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Western-US"
# DATASET_NAME="Hawaii_testset"
# DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset-subset"
DATASET_NAME="Northeastern-US_testset"


#### audio folder and labels inside datasets/${DATASET_NAME} #####
AUDIO_DIR="datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/soundscape_data"
LABELS_CSV="datasets/${DATASET_NAME}/annotations.csv"


#### select model #####
MODEL_PATH="models/Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
# MODEL_PATH="models/Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt"


#### select the species mapping (according to dataset and model) #####
SPECIES_MAPPING="Just-Bird"
# SPECIES_MAPPING="Birds-With-Labels"


#### toggle single class mode (true for Just-Bird) #####
USE_SINGLE_CLS=true
# USE_SINGLE_CLS=false


#### select output path #####
OUTPUT_PATH="results/Just-Bird"
# OUTPUT_PATH="results/Birds-With-Labels"


#########################################################################
# The most important parameters are already set via the script variables.
# But details like IoU threshold, 
# merge settings, etc. can be changed below this heading.
# To skip entire steps (for instance the confusion matrix) 
# just uncomment the respective lines.
#########################################################################


SINGLE_CLS_FLAG=()
if [ "${USE_SINGLE_CLS}" = true ]; then
    SINGLE_CLS_FLAG+=(--single-cls)
fi

# Merge settings for steps 2 and 3. Empty keeps the model's defaults:
# window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap for Just-Bird and Birds-With-Labels.
MERGE_FLAGS=()
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap 0)    # window fusion: one box per call
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--phrase-gap 0.3)  # window fusion: longer phrase boxes
# MERGE_FLAGS=(--merge reconstruct --song-gap 0.2)  # song merge: join songs across longer pauses

# Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and 
# --no-merge to get raw (unmerged) detections.
# This matches the filter-then-merge policy when 
# later filtering at each confidence threshold.
echo "Running inference (raw detections, no merge)..."
python src/inference/detect_birds.py \
    --audio "${AUDIO_DIR}" \
    --model "${MODEL_PATH}" \
    --species-mapping "${SPECIES_MAPPING}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-format json-with-algorithm-metadata \
    --conf 0.001 \
    --no-merge \
    --nms-iou 0.8 \
    --num-workers 4


# Step 2: F-beta analysis on raw detections: 
# at each confidence threshold we filter then merge.
echo "Running F-beta score analysis (filter-then-merge per threshold)..."
python src/evaluation/f_beta_score_analysis.py \
    --raw-detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --labels "${LABELS_CSV}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}/f_1.0_score_analysis" \
    --beta 1.0 \
    --iou-threshold 0.25 \
    "${MERGE_FLAGS[@]}" \
    --num-workers 8 \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"


# Step 3: From raw detections, filter at the model's default confidence
# (0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.21 for Birds-With-Labels, add --conf to change it) and merge.
echo "Filtering raw detections at the model's default confidence and merging for confusion matrix..."
python src/evaluation/filter_and_merge_detections.py \
    --raw-detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --output-format all \
    "${MERGE_FLAGS[@]}"


# Step 4: Run confusion matrix analysis.
echo "Running confusion matrix analysis..."
python src/evaluation/confusion_matrix_analysis.py \
    --detections "${OUTPUT_PATH}" \
    --labels "${LABELS_CSV}" \
    --output-path "${OUTPUT_PATH}/confusion_matrix_analysis" \
    --iou-threshold 0.25 \
    "${SINGLE_CLS_FLAG[@]}"


# Step 5: Examine results in results/ directory
echo
echo "All tasks completed!"
echo "Results can now be examined in the ${OUTPUT_PATH} directory."

If PowerShell refuses to run the script, see the execution policy note in the Installation Commands.

#Requires -Version 5.1
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#
# Default BirdBox workflow: detect birds and evaluate against labels.
# Same as run_pipeline.sh / run_pipeline.bat; pick your shell.
# Skip run_hpo.sh unless you need the advanced merge-parameter search.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

# Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
# If .venv is missing, script uses python from PATH.
if (Test-Path ".venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1") {
    Write-Host "Activating .venv"
    . ".venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1"
}


#### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####
# Just-Bird trained on the train and test splits of every regional dataset,
# so its scores on these test sets are in-domain.
# $DATASET_NAME = "Birds-With-Labels_testset"
# $DATASET_NAME = "Western-US"
# $DATASET_NAME = "Hawaii_testset"
# $DATASET_NAME = "Northeastern-US_testset-subset"
$DATASET_NAME = "Northeastern-US_testset"


#### audio folder and labels inside datasets\$DATASET_NAME #####
$AUDIO_DIR = "datasets\$DATASET_NAME\soundscape_data"
$LABELS_CSV = "datasets\$DATASET_NAME\annotations.csv"


#### select model #####
$MODEL_PATH = "models\Just-Bird_fp32.pt"
# $MODEL_PATH = "models\Birds-With-Labels_fp32.pt"


#### select the species mapping (according to dataset and model) #####
$SPECIES_MAPPING = "Just-Bird"
# $SPECIES_MAPPING = "Birds-With-Labels"


#### toggle single class mode ($true for Just-Bird) #####
$USE_SINGLE_CLS = $true
# $USE_SINGLE_CLS = $false


#### select output path #####
$OUTPUT_PATH = "results\Just-Bird"
# $OUTPUT_PATH = "results\Birds-With-Labels"


#########################################################################
# The most important parameters are already set via the script variables.
# But details like IoU threshold,
# merge settings, etc. can be changed below this heading.
# To skip entire steps (for instance the confusion matrix)
# just uncomment the respective lines.
#########################################################################


$SINGLE_CLS_FLAG = @()
if ($USE_SINGLE_CLS) { $SINGLE_CLS_FLAG = @("--single-cls") }

# Merge settings for steps 2 and 3. Empty keeps the model's defaults:
# window fusion with a 0.05 s phrase gap for Just-Bird and Birds-With-Labels.
$MERGE_FLAGS = @()
# $MERGE_FLAGS = @("--phrase-gap", "0")    # window fusion: one box per call
# $MERGE_FLAGS = @("--phrase-gap", "0.3")  # window fusion: longer phrase boxes
# $MERGE_FLAGS = @("--merge", "reconstruct", "--song-gap", "0.2")  # song merge: join songs across longer pauses

# Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and
# --no-merge to get raw (unmerged) detections.
# This matches the filter-then-merge policy when
# later filtering at each confidence threshold.
Write-Host "Running inference (raw detections, no merge)..."
python src\inference\detect_birds.py `
    --audio "$AUDIO_DIR" `
    --model "$MODEL_PATH" `
    --species-mapping "$SPECIES_MAPPING" `
    --output-path "$OUTPUT_PATH" `
    --output-format json-with-algorithm-metadata `
    --conf 0.001 `
    --no-merge `
    --nms-iou 0.8 `
    --num-workers 4


# Step 2: F-beta analysis on raw detections:
# at each confidence threshold we filter then merge.
Write-Host "Running F-beta score analysis (filter-then-merge per threshold)..."
python src\evaluation\f_beta_score_analysis.py `
    --raw-detections "$OUTPUT_PATH" `
    --labels "$LABELS_CSV" `
    --output-path "$OUTPUT_PATH\f_1.0_score_analysis" `
    --beta 1.0 `
    --iou-threshold 0.25 `
    @MERGE_FLAGS `
    --num-workers 8 `
    @SINGLE_CLS_FLAG


# Step 3: From raw detections, filter at the model's default confidence
# (0.15 for Just-Bird, 0.2 for Birds-With-Labels; add --conf to change it) and merge.
Write-Host "Filtering raw detections at the model's default confidence and merging for confusion matrix..."
python src\evaluation\filter_and_merge_detections.py `
    --raw-detections "$OUTPUT_PATH" `
    --output-path "$OUTPUT_PATH" `
    --output-format all `
    @MERGE_FLAGS


# # Step 4: Run confusion matrix analysis.
Write-Host "Running confusion matrix analysis..."
python src\evaluation\confusion_matrix_analysis.py `
    --detections "$OUTPUT_PATH" `
    --labels "$LABELS_CSV" `
    --output-path "$OUTPUT_PATH\confusion_matrix_analysis" `
    --iou-threshold 0.25 `
    @SINGLE_CLS_FLAG


# Step 5: Examine results in results\ directory
Write-Host ""
Write-Host "All tasks completed!"
Write-Host "Results can now be examined in the $OUTPUT_PATH directory."

@echo off
REM SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 BirdNET-Team
REM SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
REM Default BirdBox workflow: detect birds and evaluate against labels.
REM Same as run_pipeline.sh / run_pipeline.ps1; pick your shell.
REM Skip run_hpo.sh unless you need the advanced merge-parameter search.

setlocal EnableExtensions EnableDelayedExpansion

REM Exit if any command fails
set "FAILED=0"

REM Optional: activate local virtual environment if present.
REM If .venv is missing, script uses python from PATH.
if exist ".venv\Scripts\activate.bat" (

)


REM #### select the dataset on which inference shall be performed #####

REM Step 1: Run inference with low confidence and
REM --no-merge to get raw (unmerged) detections.
REM This matches the filter-then-merge policy when

echo Running inference (raw detections, no merge)...
python src\inference\detect_birds.py ^
    --audio "%AUDIO_DIR%" ^
    --model "%MODEL_PATH%" ^
    --species-mapping "%SPECIES_MAPPING%" ^

if errorlevel 1 goto :fail

REM at each confidence threshold we filter then merge.

python src\evaluation\f_beta_score_analysis.py ^
    --raw-detections "%OUTPUT_PATH%" ^
    --labels "%LABELS_CSV%" ^

    --beta 1.0 ^
    --iou-threshold 0.25 ^
    %MERGE_FLAGS% ^
    --num-workers 8 ^
